definition_zh: 熟练的；灵巧的；机敏的
definition_en: clever and skillful, especially in using the hands or the mind
core_image: 一只手在窄口瓶里稳稳夹出一枚硬币，稳、准、不慌
scene: 钟表铺里老师傅戴着放大镜调校游丝，手一点不抖。The adroit watchmaker fixed the tiny spring in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 adroit 是「熟练的、手艺灵巧的」（第 1 个义项：手艺或动作上的灵巧）；句意为技艺娴熟的钟表匠几秒钟就修好了细小的游丝。

collocations.zh: 一步妙棋；一次机敏的举动

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「熟练；机敏」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「熟练地；巧妙地」

senses.title: Skillful with hands or in craft
senses.definition: physically skillful, especially with the hands or in a craft
senses.definitionCN: 手上的或手艺上的灵巧熟练，尤其指动手能力
senses.example: The adroit surgeon sewed the delicate vessel closed.
senses.exampleCN: 技艺娴熟的外科医生把纤细的血管缝合好了。
senses.why: French à droit means 'according to the right hand', and the right hand is the traditional image of manual skill.
senses.whyCN: 法语 à droit 意为「按右手」，右手传统上就是手艺灵巧的象征，所以本义落在手上的功夫。

senses.title: Clever in handling situations
senses.definition: showing cleverness and resourcefulness in dealing with people or problems
senses.definitionCN: 在待人处事上表现出的机智与干练
senses.example: She was adroit at turning hostile questions back on the reporter.
senses.exampleCN: 她很老练，能把记者的刁钻问题原样抛回去。
senses.why: Skill of the hand extends by metaphor to skill of the mind: steering a conversation like steering a tool.
senses.whyCN: 手上的本领经隐喻引申为头脑的本领：像操控工具一样操控局面与谈话。

intro.en: Adroit comes from French adroit, literally 'according to the right', from the phrase à droit.
intro.cn: adroit 来自法语 adroit，字面意思是「按右手」，源自短语 à droit。

items.en: Latin directus meant 'straight, right, set upright', the past participle of dirigere, 'to set straight'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 directus 意为「直的、正的」，是动词 dirigere（摆正）的过去分词。

items.en: Old French droit meant 'right, straight', later also 'the right hand'.
items.cn: 古法语 droit 意为「正、直」，后来也指「右手」。

items.en: The phrase à droit, 'by the right (hand)', became the adjective adroit.
items.cn: 短语 à droit（用右手）凝固成形容词 adroit。

items.en: English borrowed adroit first for manual dexterity, then for mental quickness.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 adroit，先指手上的灵巧，再引申为头脑的机敏。

items.en: Today adroit covers both physical deftness and tactical cleverness.
items.cn: 现代英语中 adroit 同时涵盖手脚利索与手腕高明两重意思。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar sound or same Latin family; the second gathers near synonyms of skillfulness.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写发音相近或同属拉丁词族的词；第二组收表示「熟练、灵巧」的近义词。

entries.definition: Skillful with the hands; from Latin dexter, 'right hand', a parallel image not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灵巧的」；来自拉丁语 dexter（右手），意象相同但词源不同，并非同源。

entries.definition: To decorate; only the spelling is close, the root has nothing to do with adroit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装饰」；只是拼写与 adroit 相近，词源毫无关系。

entries.definition: From Latin directus, the same participle that gave adroit its droit element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「直接的；指挥」；与 adroit 共享拉丁语 directus 这一来源。

entries.definition: Quick and neat in movement, usually on a small scale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灵巧的、麻利的」，多指小动作上的利落。

entries.definition: Highly skilled through practice, often in a field of expertise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内行的、擅长的」，强调经练习达到的专精。

entries.definition: Shrewd and careful in dealing with practical matters.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精明的、谨慎的」，偏重处世的算计。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the right-hand root and the craftsman scene; the abstract hooks picture steady hands and quick minds.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「右手」词根与匠人场景；抽象记忆点想象稳的手与快的脑。

normal.en: French à droit literally means 'to the right (hand)'.
normal.cn: 法语 à droit 字面是「往右手」.

normal.en: The right hand is the old symbol of skill.
normal.cn: 右手自古是灵巧的象征。

normal.en: Adroit and direct share Latin directus.
normal.cn: adroit 与 direct 同享拉丁语 directus。

normal.en: The adverb adroitly marks a clever move.
normal.cn: 副词 adroitly 标记一次机敏的行动。

normal.en: The noun adroitness names the quality itself.
normal.cn: 名词 adroitness 指这份灵巧本身。

abstract.en: Picture fingers lifting a coin from a narrow bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象手指从窄瓶里稳稳夹出一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a debater turning the question around like a tool.
abstract.cn: 想象辩手把问题像工具一样转了个方向。

abstract.en: Picture a right hand leading, the left following.
abstract.cn: 想象右手引路、左手跟随。

examples.en: The adroit watchmaker fixed the tiny spring in seconds.
examples.cn: 技艺娴熟的钟表匠几秒钟就修好了细小的游丝。

examples.en: An adroit reply saved the interview from disaster.
examples.cn: 一句机敏的回答把访谈从尴尬里救了回来。

examples.en: She is adroit at defusing arguments with humor.
examples.cn: 她擅长用幽默化解争执。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额准」——额头上写着「准」字，手稳心细，出手就是又快又准的熟练。

root: 拉丁语 dirigere（摆正）→ directus（直的、正的）→ 古法语 droit（正、右手）→ 法语短语 à droit（用右手）；核心义是「像用惯用的右手那样顺手」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from skill of the hands to cleverness in handling people and situations.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从手上的灵巧，走到待人接物上的机敏老练。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady right hand that never fumbles
core.cn: 核心意象：一只从不失手的右手

branches.en: The hand that works neatly and fast.
branches.cn: 干得又利落又快的那双手。

branches.en: The mind that steers talk like a tool.
branches.cn: 像使工具一样驾驭谈话的头脑。

branches.en: Both senses mean doing the right thing with ease.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指轻松做对事情。

branches.en: Politics rewards the adroit above the honest.
branches.cn: 政治场上老练比老实更吃香。

branches.en: Surgeons and watchmakers typify this sense.
branches.cn: 外科医生与钟表匠是这个义项的典型。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin right-root direct/droit with the French phrase frame à, and the family gives direct and dirge-free relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「正、直」词根 direct/droit 与法语短语框 à，同族词还有 direct。

latinIntro.en: Latin directus and dirigere are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 directus 与 dirigere 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 谄媚的；阿谀奉承的；吹捧的
definition_en: full of excessive praise meant to please someone important
core_image: 下属弯着腰，把一堆好听的话像糖果一样捧到上司面前
scene: 庆功宴上经理刚举杯，周围已经是一片夸赞声。The adulatory speech praised the manager far beyond his real contribution.
sceneCN: 这里 adulatory 是「谄媚的、吹捧过头的」（第 1 个义项：言辞上过分讨好的）；句意为奉承的致辞把经理夸得远超他实际的功劳。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去 -ory 加名词后缀构成，义为「吹捧；谄媚」
动词原形，义为「谄媚；奉承」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「谄媚者」

senses.title: Excessively flattering in words
senses.definition: expressing admiration that is excessive and meant to please
senses.definitionCN: 表达出过分的赞美，目的是讨好对方
senses.example: The adulatory review read like an advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇吹捧的评论读起来像广告。
senses.why: The Latin root adulari means 'to fawn like a dog', so the core image is a dog wagging itself into favor.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 adulari 意为「像狗一样摇尾」，核心意象就是摇尾巴讨好人。

senses.title: Servile in manner toward the powerful
senses.definition: showing a servile, fawning attitude toward someone powerful
senses.definitionCN: 对有权势者表现出的低姿态与讨好
senses.example: The staff's adulatory behavior around the chairman made the visitors uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 员工们在董事长身边那副阿谀的姿态让访客很不舒服。
senses.why: Fawning in words extends to the whole posture: the body language of a courtier.
senses.whyCN: 言辞上的摇尾延伸到整个姿态：廷臣式的肢体语言。

intro.en: Adulatory comes from Latin adulatio, 'fawning', from the verb adulari, 'to fawn like a dog'.
intro.cn: adulatory 来自拉丁语 adulatio（谄媚），动词原形是 adulari（像狗一样摇尾讨好）。

items.en: Adulari meant 'to flatter, to fawn'; its origin within Latin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 adulari 意为「奉承、讨好」；它在拉丁语内部的来源不确定。

items.en: Adulatio was the noun for fawning behavior, common in descriptions of court life.
items.cn: 名词 adulatio 指谄媚行为，常见于对宫廷生活的描写。

items.en: English took adulation and adulatory from Latin in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪从拉丁语借入 adulation 与 adulatory。

items.en: The adjective settled into reviews, biographies and political writing for empty praise.
items.cn: 十九世纪前，该形容词固定用于书评、传记与政论文中的空洞吹捧。

items.en: Adulatory now almost always carries a critical tone, suggesting insincere praise.
items.cn: 现代英语中 adulatory 几乎总带贬义，暗示赞美并不真诚。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers near synonyms of flattery.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收表示「奉承、讨好」的近义词。

entries.definition: A grown person; only the first letters match, the root is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「成年人；成年的」；只是开头字母与 adulatory 相近，词源完全无关。

entries.definition: To make impure by mixing; shares the ad- prefix only, the rest is a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「掺假」；与 adulatory 只共享前缀 ad-，词干来源不同。

entries.definition: Deep worship or love; the meanings both involve praise, but the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇敬；爱慕」；虽然同样涉及赞美，但词源与 adulatory 无关。

entries.definition: Flattering powerful people for personal gain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谄媚的」，强调为私利讨好权贵。

entries.definition: Servile in manner, eager to obey and please.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「卑躬屈膝的」，偏重姿态上的低声下气。

entries.definition: Showing servile affection, like a dog greeting its master.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「摇尾乞怜的」，保留词源中狗的意象。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fawning-dog root and the flattery scene; the abstract hooks picture wagging tails and honeyed words.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「摇尾狗」词根与奉承场景；抽象记忆点想象摇动的尾巴与抹了蜜的话。

normal.en: Latin adulari means 'to fawn like a dog'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulari 意为「像狗一样讨好」。

normal.en: Adulation is the noun for such praise.
normal.cn: adulation 是这种吹捧的名词。

normal.en: Adulate is the plain verb form.
normal.cn: adulate 是朴素的动词形式。

normal.en: The ending -ory makes it an adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ory 使它成为形容词。

normal.en: Adulatory praise is never sincere.
normal.cn: adulatory 式的赞美从不真诚。

abstract.en: Picture a dog wagging so hard it spins.
abstract.cn: 想象一条狗摇尾巴摇得原地打转。

abstract.en: Picture a speech dripping with syrup.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇淋满糖浆的致辞。

abstract.en: Picture medals handed out before the work is judged.
abstract.cn: 想象作品还没评审、奖章已经发完。

examples.en: The adulatory speech praised the manager far beyond his real contribution.
examples.cn: 奉承的致辞把经理夸得远超他实际的功劳。

examples.en: Critics dismissed the biography as adulatory and shallow.
examples.cn: 评论家批评这本传记一味歌功颂德、内容肤浅。

examples.en: He grew suspicious of the adulatory tone of the new assistant.
examples.cn: 新助教那副阿谀的腔调让他起了疑心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额丢料」——额头都丢出去了（磕头），材料全没了，只剩一肚子奉承话。

root: 拉丁语 adulari（摇尾讨好，来源不确定）→ adulatio（谄媚）→ 英语 adulation / adulatory；核心义是「像狗讨主人那样的赞美」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from flattering words to the servile manner behind them.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从言辞上的吹捧，走到背后那副讨好的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog fawning at its master's feet
core.cn: 核心意象：趴在主人脚边摇尾的狗

branches.en: Praise poured far beyond the truth.
branches.cn: 远远越过事实的赞美。

branches.en: The bent posture behind the words.
branches.cn: 话语背后弯下去的腰。

branches.en: Both senses trade dignity for favor.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在用尊严换好处。

branches.en: Reviews and speeches are its usual stage.
branches.cn: 书评与致辞是它常见的舞台。

branches.en: Courts and offices breed this manner.
branches.cn: 宫廷与职场滋生这种姿态。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin flattering root adul- with the adjective ending -ory, and the family gives adulation and adulate.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「讨好」词根 adul- 与形容词尾 -ory，同族词有 adulation 与 adulate。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulari and adulatio are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulari 与 adulatio 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 掺杂物；掺假用的物质
definition_en: a substance added to something to make it impure or of lower quality
core_image: 一勺白粉悄悄混进整袋奶粉里，袋子没变重多少，东西却坏了
scene: 化验员把样本放进仪器，屏幕上跳出一条多余的曲线。The lab found an adulterant mixed into the chili powder.
sceneCN: 这里 adulterant 是「掺杂物」（第 1 个义项：被故意混进去以降低纯度的物质）；句意为实验室在辣椒粉里检出了掺杂物。

derivatives.zh: 动词基础形式，义为「掺假；使不纯」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「掺假行为；掺杂」
由动词过去分词转形容词，义为「掺了假的」

senses.title: Substance that spoils purity
senses.definition: a foreign substance mixed into a food, drug or material to make it cheaper or heavier
senses.definitionCN: 混进食品、药品或原料中使其变便宜或变重的外来物质
senses.example: Water is the cheapest adulterant in milk.
senses.exampleCN: 水是牛奶里最便宜的掺杂物。
senses.why: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute', so an adulterant is literally a polluting ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」，所以 adulterant 字面上就是污染性成分。

senses.title: Describing such a substance
senses.definition: serving to adulterate; used of a substance that makes something impure
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容起掺假作用的物质
senses.example: The inspector listed the adulterant agents used by the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员列出了该工厂使用的掺假物质。
senses.why: The noun sense extends into a modifier: the substance defined by its dirty job.
senses.whyCN: 名词义扩展为修饰语：这种物质以它干的脏活来定义。

intro.en: Adulterant comes from Latin adulterare, 'to pollute, to corrupt', from adulter, 'spurious, impure'.
intro.cn: adulterant 来自拉丁语 adulterare（污染、败坏），词根是 adulter（假的、不纯的）。

items.en: Adulter meant 'adulterated, spurious', formed with the prefix ad-, 'toward', on a root meaning 'to pollute'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 adulter 意为「掺假的、假冒的」，由前缀 ad-（朝向）加表示「污染」的词干构成。

items.en: Adulterare was the verb 'to corrupt, to make impure', used of goods and of morals.
items.cn: 动词 adulterare 意为「败坏、使不纯」，既用于货物也用于道德。

items.en: English adopted adulterate in the sixteenth century for corrupting goods.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 adulterate，指对货物做手脚。

items.en: As food regulation grew, adulterant named the specific polluting substance.
items.cn: 随着食品法规兴起，adulterant 专指污染性物质本身。

items.en: Today adulterant appears mostly in food, drug and forensic contexts.
items.cn: 如今 adulterant 多出现在食品、药品与司法检验语境中。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers related impurity words.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收与「不纯、污染」相关的词。

entries.definition: A grown person; the shared opening is accidental, the roots are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；开头拼写碰巧相同，词源无关。

entries.definition: Flattering in an excessive way; similar shape, different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谄媚的」；词形相近，但拉丁词根不同。

entries.definition: The verb from which adulterant is derived; to mix in an impure substance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，adulterant 的来源动词，义为「掺假」。

entries.definition: A polluting substance, usually introduced accidentally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「污染物」，多指无意混入。

entries.definition: Any substance that makes a material impure.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杂质」，泛指使不纯的成分。

entries.definition: A cheap substance used to bulk out a product.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「填充物」，指用来增量的廉价成分。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pollute root and the lab scene; the abstract hooks picture a white powder and a guilty spoon.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「污染」词根与化验场景；抽象记忆点想象一勺白粉。

normal.en: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」。

normal.en: Adulterate is the verb, adulterant the agent.
normal.cn: adulterate 是动词，adulterant 是那个东西。

normal.en: Adulteration names the practice itself.
normal.cn: adulteration 指掺假这种行径。

normal.en: Adulterated milk is milk with an adulterant.
normal.cn: 掺假牛奶就是混了掺杂物的牛奶。

normal.en: The plural adulterants lists them all.
normal.cn: 复数 adulterants 把它们一并列出。

abstract.en: Picture one bad spoonful spoiling the whole sack.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺坏东西毁掉一整袋。

abstract.en: Picture a lab curve jumping where it should not.
abstract.cn: 想象化验曲线在不该跳的地方跳了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a scale tipped with cheap powder.
abstract.cn: 想象天平被廉价粉末压偏。

examples.en: The lab found an adulterant mixed into the chili powder.
examples.cn: 实验室在辣椒粉里检出了掺杂物。

examples.en: Regulators ban any adulterant that threatens health.
examples.cn: 监管机构禁止任何危害健康的掺杂物。

examples.en: Adulterants make cheap goods look like the real thing.
examples.cn: 掺杂物让廉价货看起来像真货。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额特料」——额外加的料，就是那点见不得光的掺假物。

root: 拉丁语 adulter（假的、不纯的）→ adulterare（污染、败坏）→ 英语 adulterate / adulterant；核心义是「把好东西弄脏的那一点外来物」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the polluting substance itself to its use as a describing word.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从污染性物质本身，走到它作修饰语的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foreign powder slipped into a clean sack
core.cn: 核心意象：偷偷混进净袋里的一把外来粉末

branches.en: The substance that does the dirtying.
branches.cn: 干脏活的那种物质。

branches.en: The word describing any such substance.
branches.cn: 形容这类物质的用语。

branches.en: Both senses center on ruined purity.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕被破坏的纯度。

branches.en: Food and drug tests hunt it down.
branches.cn: 食品药品检测专门缉拿它。

branches.en: Water, starch and dye are classic cases.
branches.cn: 水、淀粉与染料是经典案例。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin pollute root adulter- with the agent ending -ant, and the family gives adulterate and adulteration.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「污染」词根 adulter- 与施动尾 -ant，同族词有 adulterate 与 adulteration。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulter and adulterare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulter 与 adulterare 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 掺假；使不纯；败坏
definition_en: to make something impure or lower in quality by adding another substance
core_image: 一滴墨汁落进清水瓶，整瓶水再也回不到从前
scene: 作坊老板背对着门，把便宜油倒进贵油罐。The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
sceneCN: 这里 adulterate 是「掺假、使不纯」（第 1 个义项：往好东西里混入次等物）；句意为商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「掺假；掺杂」
由动词派生的施动名词，义为「掺杂物」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「掺假者」

senses.title: Make goods impure by mixing
senses.definition: to lower the quality of food, drink or goods by adding inferior substances
senses.definitionCN: 往食品、饮品或货物里加入次等物质以降低其品质
senses.example: The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
senses.exampleCN: 商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。
senses.why: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute', so the core image is corrupting something clean by pouring into it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」，核心意象就是往干净东西里灌入脏东西。

senses.title: Corrupt something abstract
senses.definition: to weaken or spoil the purity of an idea, language or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 使观念、语言或传统失去纯粹
senses.example: Critics said the sequel adulterated the spirit of the original film.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者说续集败坏了原作的精神。
senses.why: Mixing inferior matter extends by metaphor to ideas: the pure original gets watered down.
senses.whyCN: 掺次等物的动作经隐喻引申到观念：纯粹的原型被稀释。

senses.title: Adjective: impure, debased
senses.definition: describing something that has been made impure or of lower quality
senses.definitionCN: 形容已被掺假或品质下降的东西
senses.example: The customs office seized sacks of adulterate saffron.
senses.exampleCN: 海关查获了几袋掺假藏红花。
senses.why: The past participle hardens into an adjective: the result-state of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词凝固为形容词：动词造成的结果状态。

intro.en: Adulterate comes from Latin adulterare, 'to pollute, to corrupt', built on adulter, 'spurious, impure'.
intro.cn: adulterate 来自拉丁语 adulterare（污染、败坏），词根是 adulter（假的、不纯的）。

items.en: The root adulter described anything spurious, mixed, or not what it claimed to be.
items.cn: 词根 adulter 形容一切假冒的、掺混的、名不副实的东西。

items.en: Adulterare was the verb 'to corrupt'; ancient writers used it of wine, metals and morals alike.
items.cn: 动词 adulterare 意为「败坏」；古代作家用它形容酒、金属与道德。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century, first of corrupted goods.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入该动词，最初用于被做手脚的货物。

items.en: The adjective use for 'impure' settled beside the verb.
items.cn: 十七世纪，「不纯的」形容词用法在动词旁定型。

items.en: Modern use stresses commercial fraud, with the adjective common in customs and lab reports.
items.cn: 现代用法强调商业欺诈，形容词常见于海关与化验报告。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers near synonyms of corrupting and diluting.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收表示「败坏、稀释」的近义词。

entries.definition: A grown person; only the opening letters are shared, the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；只是开头字母相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: Marital unfaithfulness; from the same Latin adulter, corrupted fidelity rather than corrupted goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通奸」；出自同一拉丁词根 adulter，是「被败坏的忠诚」而非「被败坏的货物」。

entries.definition: Excessive flattery; close in sound, unrelated in root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吹捧」；发音接近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To make something dirty or unsafe, often by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「污染」，多指无意间弄脏。

entries.definition: To lower the value or status of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「贬低；使劣化」，偏重价值与地位。

entries.definition: To weaken by mixing with water or another thinning agent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「稀释；冲淡」，是掺假的一种具体方式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pollute root and the oil-seller scene; the abstract hooks picture ink in water and a lowered grade.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「污染」词根与卖油人场景；抽象记忆点想象水中的墨与降级的货。

normal.en: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」。

normal.en: Adulterant is the thing, adulterate the act.
normal.cn: adulterant 是物，adulterate 是行为。

normal.en: Adulteration is the crime's name in law.
normal.cn: adulteration 是法律上这种罪行的名字。

normal.en: Adulterated goods fail customs tests.
normal.cn: 掺假货物过不了海关检验。

normal.en: Adultery shares the root but means unfaithfulness.
normal.cn: adultery 同根但指不忠。

abstract.en: Picture ink spreading through a bottle of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象墨汁在一瓶清水里晕开。

abstract.en: Picture gold coins shaved and refilled with copper.
abstract.cn: 想象金币被削去一角补上铜。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe ruined by one cheap shortcut.
abstract.cn: 想象一道菜谱被一个廉价的偷工步骤毁掉。

examples.en: The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
examples.cn: 商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。

examples.en: It is illegal to adulterate milk with water for sale.
examples.cn: 往牛奶里掺水出售是违法的。

examples.en: Years of careless edits adulterated the original text.
examples.cn: 多年草率的编辑败坏了原文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额特喂」——额外地喂进去一些假料，好东西就被败坏了。

root: 拉丁语 adulter（假的、不纯的）→ adulterare（污染、败坏）→ 英语 adulterate；核心义是「把干净的弄脏、把纯的变假」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from mixing impurities into goods, to corrupting abstract things, to the adjective for the result.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从给货物掺假，到败坏抽象事物，再到形容结果的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink falling into clear water
core.cn: 核心意象：落入清水的一滴墨

branches.en: Goods spoiled by what was slipped into them.
branches.cn: 被偷偷混入的次等物毁掉的货物。

branches.en: Ideas and traditions watered down.
branches.cn: 被稀释变味的观念与传统。

branches.en: The finished state: already impure.
branches.cn: 完成时的状态：已然不纯。

branches.en: Both senses trade purity for cheapness.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在用纯度换廉价。

branches.en: Customs and labs test for it daily.
branches.cn: 海关与化验室天天检验它。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin pollute root adulter- with the verb ending -ate, and the family gives adulteration and adulterant.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「污染」词根 adulter- 与动词尾 -ate，同族词有 adulteration 与 adulterant。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulter and adulterare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulter 与 adulterare 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；利益；（网球）占先
definition_en: something that puts you in a better position, or a benefit gained from a situation
core_image: 两个人赛跑，一个站在下坡，一个站在上坡
scene: 同样的价格，这家店出门就是地铁，那家要转两趟车。Living near the station is a real advantage.
sceneCN: 这里的 advantage 是「有利条件」（第 1 个义项：使人处于更有利位置的因素）；句意是住在车站附近是个实实在在的优势。

pos.zh: 名词：优势；有利条件；利益；（网球）占先

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「不利条件；劣势」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有利的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「有利地」
由名词加分词后缀构成，义为「处于有利地位的」

senses.title: A condition that puts you ahead
senses.definition: a circumstance or quality that gives someone a better chance than others
senses.definitionCN: 使某人比他人更有机会的处境或特质
senses.example: Her fluent Spanish gave her an advantage in the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她流利的西班牙语让她在面试中占了优势。
senses.why: Old French avantage came from avant, before: an advantage is a position slightly ahead of the others.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avantage 出自 avant（在前）：优势就是比他人稍稍靠前的位置。

senses.title: A benefit gained
senses.definition: a useful or favourable result that comes from something
senses.definitionCN: 由某事带来的有用或有利的结果
senses.example: We should take advantage of the fine weather.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应该利用这段好天气。
senses.why: Being ahead is useful, and the word slides from the lead itself to the gain it brings.
senses.whyCN: 领先本身有用，于是词义从「领先的位置」滑到「由此得到的好处」。

senses.title: The point after deuce in tennis
senses.definition: the first point won after deuce, which puts a player one point from the game
senses.definitionCN: 平局后赢下的第一分，使球员距赢下该局只差一分
senses.example: The player held advantage after the long rally.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间多拍回合之后，这名球员保持着占先。
senses.why: Tennis uses the old idea of being ahead: after deuce, one player stands one point in front.
senses.whyCN: 网球沿用「领先」这一旧义：平局之后，一方只比别人多出一分。

intro.en: The noun of being in front, from Latin before.
intro.cn: 一个表示「在前」的名词，出自拉丁语的「前」。

items.en: ante meant before or in front of.
items.cn: ante 意为在……之前、在……前面。

items.en: abante, from before, gave the French words for moving ahead.
items.cn: abante（从前面）生出法语中表示前移的词。

items.en: avant meant before or in front, and avantage meant a place in front.
items.cn: avant 意为在前，avantage 指「靠前的位置」。

items.en: English adopted advantage for a favourable position in a contest.
items.cn: 英语借入 advantage，指竞争中有利的位置。

items.en: Business added competitive advantage, and tennis gave the word a fixed scoring sense.
items.cn: 商业添上 competitive advantage，网球则给它一个固定的计分义。

note.en: The first group is the avant family; the second gathers words for a lead and for benefit.
note.cn: 第一组是 avant 词族；第二组收领先与好处两类词。

entries.definitionCN: 微弱优势

abstract.cn: 想象两个跑者，一个站在下坡起跑。

abstract.en: Picture a shop right at the station exit.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店就开在地铁出口。

abstract.en: Think of a tennis scoreboard showing one point in front.
abstract.cn: 想象网球记分牌上领先一分。

examples.cn: 她流利的西班牙语让她在面试中占了优势。

sensesIntro.cn: 「处在前面」这一点，管着竞争、生意与网球记分牌。

core.cn: 核心意象：一个跑者起跑时领先半步。

branches.en: a candidate with a second language
branches.cn: 会第二语言的应聘者

branches.en: a shop beside the station exit
branches.cn: 开在地铁出口旁的店

branches.en: good weather put to use
branches.cn: 被利用起来的好天气

branches.en: a tennis score one point ahead
branches.cn: 网球里领先一分

branches.en: the lead and the gain it brings
branches.cn: 领先的位置与它带来的好处

intro.en: A French noun of being in front, with a Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: 一个表示「在前」的法语名词，祖上是拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: ante is also the source of anticipate and anterior.
latinIntro.cn: ante 也是 anticipate 与 anterior 的来源。

definition_zh: 有利的；有益的；有好处的
definition_en: producing a benefit or a better position; helpful to a plan or a person
core_image: 一股风正好推在你背后，让你省下半程力气
scene: 帆船赛前，老水手抬头看云，把舵柄交给徒弟。A steady offshore wind was advantageous for the smaller boat.
sceneCN: 这里 advantageous 是「有利的」（第 1 个义项：能带来好处或更好处境的）；句意为稳定的离岸风对小船有利。图中可辨识的物件：帆、舵柄、海面上的白浪。

pos.zh: 有利的；有益的；有好处的

derivatives.zh: 本形容词的名词基础，义为「优势；有利条件」
由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有利地；有益地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利的」

senses.title: Producing a benefit
senses.definition: bringing a gain or making a situation better
senses.definitionCN: 带来收益或使处境变得更好
senses.example: Early planting is advantageous in a short growing season.
senses.exampleCN: 在生长季短的地方，早播是有利的。
senses.why: The adjective simply turns the noun advantage into a quality: whatever yields an advantage is advantageous.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词 advantage 变成一种性质：凡能带来优势的，就是 advantageous。

senses.title: Favourable to a particular person
senses.definition: helpful to one side in a specific situation, usually followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情形中对某一方有帮助，通常后接 to
senses.example: The ruling was advantageous to small landowners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决对小地主有利。
senses.why: A position is always someone's position, so the adjective naturally asks who is being helped and takes the preposition to.
senses.whyCN: 位置总是某人的位置，所以这个形容词自然会问「谁受了益」，并接上介词 to。

senses.title: Favourable in business terms
senses.definition: used of prices, terms or contracts that favour the buyer or the holder
senses.definitionCN: 用于对买方或持有人有利的价格、条款或合同
senses.example: They secured advantageous terms on the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在租约上争取到了优惠条件。
senses.why: Commerce is the modern arena where being ahead is measured in money, so the adjective attaches to terms and prices.
senses.whyCN: 商业是现代社会用金钱衡量「领先」的场域，于是这个形容词常挂在条款与价格上。

senses.title: Giving a positional edge
senses.definition: describing ground, height or placement that gives an edge in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 形容在较量中带来优势的地形、高度或位置
senses.example: The regiment held an advantageous ridge above the road.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团占据着公路旁一处有利的山脊。
senses.why: The literal image of the word is higher or better ground, and military writing keeps that image alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的字面意象就是更高或更好的地势，军事写作让这幅画面一直活着。

senses.title: Good for both sides
senses.definition: in the phrase mutually advantageous, beneficial to each party in an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在 mutually advantageous 这一说法中，指对安排中的每一方都有益
senses.example: The two ports signed a mutually advantageous customs agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两个港口签署了一份互利的海关协议。
senses.why: If advantage can be shared, the adjective can be pluralised in meaning, and diplomacy uses it to soften bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 既然优势可以共享，这个形容词在意义上就能复数化，外交语言便用它来柔化讨价还价。

senses.title: A polite word for self-serving
senses.definition: used politely of an arrangement that mainly serves the speaker's interest
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地用于一项主要服务于说话者自身利益的安排
senses.example: He called the rezoning advantageous, though only his land gained value.
senses.exampleCN: 他称这次重新分区是有利的，尽管只有他自己的地涨了价。
senses.why: Because the adjective is neutral in form, it can dress a private gain in public language, which is why it often sounds evasive.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个形容词形式上中立，它能用公共语言包装私人收益，所以常听起来像在回避。

senses.title: An adaptive edge in biology
senses.definition: in biology, describing a trait that improves an organism's chance of survival
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，形容能提高生物存活机会的性状
senses.example: A thicker coat proved advantageous during the cold snap.
senses.exampleCN: 寒潮期间，更厚的毛皮被证明是有利的。
senses.why: Evolution is a long contest, and any inherited edge is an advantage written into a body.
senses.whyCN: 演化是一场漫长的较量，任何遗传上的优势都是写进身体里的 advantage。

senses.title: A recommended option in formal prose
senses.definition: in formal writing, describing a course of action that is worth choosing
senses.definitionCN: 在正式写作中，形容值得选取的做法
senses.example: It would be advantageous to settle the matter before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 在审计之前把这件事解决掉会更为可取。
senses.why: Formal prose prefers the adjective over the blunt phrase good for you, so it becomes a polite recommendation.
senses.whyCN: 正式文字偏爱这个形容词，而不直说「对你有好处」，于是它成了一种礼貌的推荐。

intro.en: Advantageous is advantage plus the Latin adjective ending -ous; the noun beneath it comes from Old French avantage, from avant, before.
intro.cn: advantageous 是 advantage 加上拉丁形容词词尾 -ous；其下层的名词来自古法语 avantage，而 avantage 又来自 avant「在前」。

items.en: Ante meant before or in front, the oldest layer shared by the whole family.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」或「在前面」，是整个词族共享的最古一层。

items.en: Avant meant before or ahead, and it survives in English in avant-garde.
items.cn: avant 意为「在前」，至今仍活在英语的 avant-garde 里。

items.en: Avantage named a position ahead; English borrowed it as advantage.
items.cn: avantage 命名「靠前的位置」，英语借作 advantage。

items.en: The noun advantage settles in English, and the adjective is soon formed on it.
items.cn: 名词 advantage 在英语中稳定下来，形容词很快就在它上面构成。

items.en: French had its own adjective avantageux, and English -ous attaches to the borrowed stem in parallel.
items.cn: 法语本有形容词 avantageux，英语的 -ous 则平行地接在借来的词干上。

items.en: The adjective spreads into commerce, law and biology, keeping the same core of a better position.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩展到商业、法律与生物学，核心始终是「更好的位置」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advantage family with its negation and adverb; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of benefit, which differ in formality and in whether they imply comparison.
note.cn: 形近组是 advantage 词族及其否定式与副词；近义组收表示「有好处」的形容词，差别在于正式程度以及是否隐含比较。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所依附的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb, describing how something is done to one's benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述某事如何被做得对己有利。

entries.definition: The negated adjective, naming what holds a person back.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀的形容词，指拖住人的因素。

entries.definition: Producing a good effect, often used of health, policy or learning.
entries.definitionCN: 产生良好效果，常用于健康、政策或学习。

entries.definition: Showing approval or giving good conditions, broader than advantageous.
entries.definitionCN: 表示赞许或提供良好条件，范围比 advantageous 更广。

entries.definition: The plain everyday word for giving assistance, with no sense of competition.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语里表示「有帮助」的朴素说法，不含竞争意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the avant stem, the -ous ending and the prepositions and collocations the adjective actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 avant 词干、-ous 词尾，以及这个形容词实际接的介词与搭配。

normal.en: Avant means before, -age makes a state, -ous makes a quality: the state of being ahead becomes a describable quality.
normal.cn: avant 意为「在前」，-age 造成状态，-ous 造成性质：处于前面的状态变成可描述的性质。

normal.en: The adjective takes to: advantageous to the buyer, advantageous to both sides.
normal.cn: 这个形容词接 to：advantageous to the buyer、advantageous to both sides。

normal.en: Business writing likes advantageous terms and advantageous prices.
normal.cn: 商业写作偏爱 advantageous terms 与 advantageous prices。

normal.en: Mutually advantageous is the diplomatic phrase for a deal both sides can defend.
normal.cn: mutually advantageous 是外交上形容「双方都能交代的交易」的说法。

normal.en: The comparatives are more and most advantageous, not advantageouer.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级是 more advantageous 与 most advantageous，而不是 advantageouer。

abstract.en: Picture a tailwind that costs nothing and shortens the whole race.
abstract.cn: 想象一股不花分文、却缩短整场比赛的顺风。

abstract.en: The word always implies a comparison: something is better for someone than the alternative.
abstract.cn: 这个词总隐含比较：对某人来说，某事比另一种选择更好。

abstract.en: Its neutral tone is exactly what makes it useful when a private gain needs a public word.
abstract.cn: 它的中性语气，正是私人收益需要一个公共说辞时它好用的原因。

examples.en: A later start would be advantageous for the students who commute.
examples.cn: 对需要通勤的学生来说，晚一点开课会更有利。

examples.en: The treaty was advantageous to both coastal provinces.
examples.cn: 这项条约对两个沿海省份都有利。

examples.en: Reviewers found the proposal advantageous but poorly costed.
examples.cn: 评审者认为这个提案有利，但成本核算很差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德万泰杰斯」——万泰皆得，占尽便宜：有利的

root: advantage（优势，源自拉丁 abante「从前面」经古法语 avantage）+ 形容词词尾 -ous → advantageous，义为「有利的；有益的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advantageous all describe something that improves your position: a plain benefit, a favour to one side, good commercial terms, higher ground, a deal good for both, a polite name for self-interest, an adaptive trait and a formal recommendation.
sensesIntro.cn: advantageous 的八个义项都描述「改善你的处境」：单纯的好处、对某一方的偏助、优惠的商业条件、更高的地势、对双方都好的交易、对私利的礼貌称呼、适应性的性状，以及正式的推荐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wind at your back that shortens the distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股推在背后的风，把距离缩短。

branches.en: THE BENEFIT LINE: the adjective names what yields a gain, and asks for whom.
branches.cn: 收益线：这个形容词命名能带来收益之物，并追问对谁而言。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: prices and terms are the modern measure of a better position.
branches.cn: 市场线：价格与条款是现代衡量「更好位置」的尺度。

branches.en: THE EDGE LINE: from a ridge to an inherited trait, an edge is an edge.
branches.cn: 优势线：从一道山脊到一种遗传性状，优势就是优势。

branches.en: THE INTEREST LINE: advantage can be shared honestly or dressed up politely.
branches.cn: 利益线：优势可以被诚实地共享，也可以被礼貌地包装。

branches.en: THE DISCOURSE LINE: formal prose uses the adjective to recommend without insisting.
branches.cn: 话语线：正式文字用这个形容词来推荐，而不把话说死。

intro.en: Advantageous is advantage plus -ous; the noun itself is French in -age on avant, and the negating dis- and the adverb -ly complete the set.
intro.cn: advantageous 是 advantage 加 -ous；名词本身是建于 avant 之上的法语 -age 名词，否定前缀 dis- 与副词词尾 -ly 补全了这一组。

latinIntro.en: Ante and abante are attested in Latin; avant and avantage in Old French. The English endings -ous, -ly and dis- are all productive.
latinIntro.cn: ante 与 abante 在拉丁语中有文献，avant 与 avantage 在古法语中有文献；英语的 -ous、-ly 与 dis- 都仍能产。

items.example: It is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族最古老的一层。

items.example: It is the source of advantage.

items.exampleCN: 它把 advantage 变成 advantageous。

items.example: It forms the phrase mutually advantageous.

derivatives.zh: 由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有利地」
由 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利的」

definition_zh: 到来；出现；（首字母大写）基督降临节
definition_en: the arrival or first appearance of something important, especially after a long wait
core_image: 远处的地平线上终于出现一个正在靠近的黑点
scene: 天文台的观测窗前，一群人守到后半夜，屏幕上的光点终于开始变大。The advent of cheap sensors changed amateur astronomy completely.
sceneCN: 这里 advent 是「到来」（第 1 个义项：重要事物经过漫长等待后出现）；句意为廉价传感器的到来彻底改变了业余天文。图中可辨识的物件：望远镜、屏幕、保温杯。

pos.zh: 到来；出现；（大写）基督降临节

forms.label: 不可数（固定于 the advent of）

derivatives.zh: 由 Advent 加 -ist 构成，指「相信基督再临的教派成员」
由同一拉丁词根加 -itious 构成，义为「偶然外来的；非本位的」
由 Advent 加 -al 构成，义为「降临节的」

senses.title: The arrival of something long awaited
senses.definition: the arrival of an important event, thing or period after a period of waiting
senses.definitionCN: 重要的事件、事物或时期经过一段等待之后的到来
senses.example: The advent of the printing press reshaped reading in Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷机的到来重塑了欧洲的阅读方式。
senses.why: The Latin noun means an arrival, so the plainest sense is simply that something has come.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本义就是「到达」，所以最朴素的义项就是某物已经来了。

senses.title: The first appearance of a technology
senses.definition: the point at which a new tool, product or system first becomes available
senses.definitionCN: 新的工具、产品或系统首次可供使用的时点
senses.example: The advent of streaming ended the video shop on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 流媒体的出现终结了街角的录像店。
senses.why: When an invention arrives it divides time into before and after, so the word marks a boundary in history.
senses.whyCN: 一项发明到来时把时间分成前后两段，所以这个词标记的是历史上的一道分界。

senses.title: The Christian season before Christmas
senses.definition: the four weeks of preparation before Christmas in the Christian calendar
senses.definitionCN: 基督教历法中圣诞节前为期四周的准备期
senses.example: The church stays unlit during Advent until the fourth Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 降临节期间，教堂直到第四个主日才点灯。
senses.why: The season is named for a coming, because it is spent waiting for a birth that has not yet happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个节期以「到来」命名，因为它整个是在等待一件尚未发生的诞生。

senses.title: The expected return of Christ
senses.definition: in theology, the promised second coming of Christ at the end of history
senses.definitionCN: 神学中，历史终结时基督应许的第二次来临
senses.example: The sermon dwelt on the advent of the Lord in judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲道详述了主在审判中的再临。
senses.why: The same noun serves the liturgical calendar and the end of time, both being arrivals that the faithful wait for.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既服务礼仪年历，也服务时间的终点，两者都是信徒等待的来临。

senses.title: The start of a new era
senses.definition: the beginning of a new period in a field or in society
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或社会中一个新时期的开始
senses.example: Historians speak of the advent of the industrial age.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家谈到工业时代的到来。
senses.why: An arrival can be large enough to name an age, and the word then stands for the opening of a period.
senses.whyCN: 一次到来可以大到足以命名一个时代，此时这个词就代指一个时期的开端。

senses.title: A person's arrival in a role
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, the arrival of a notable person into a place or post
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，某位重要人物进入某地或某职
senses.example: The advent of a new coach lifted the whole squad.
senses.exampleCN: 新教练的到任提振了整支队伍。
senses.why: People also arrive, and formal prose borrows the grand noun to give an entrance some weight.
senses.whyCN: 人也会到达，正式文字借用这个庄重的名词，给一次登场添上分量。

senses.title: The onset of a condition
senses.definition: in medical writing, the point at which a disease or symptom begins
senses.definitionCN: 医学写作中，疾病或症状开始出现的时点
senses.example: Treatment works best before the advent of severe symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 在严重症状出现之前治疗效果最好。
senses.why: A disease arrives on its own schedule, so medicine uses the same noun for the hour it first shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 疾病按自己的时间表到来，于是医学用同一个名词指它初次露面的时刻。

senses.title: The coming of a season
senses.definition: in literary description, the arrival of a season or a natural change
senses.definitionCN: 在文学描写中，季节或自然变化的来临
senses.example: The advent of spring brought colour back to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 春天的来临让山谷重新有了颜色。
senses.why: Seasons come whether or not anyone waits, and poetry keeps the old noun for that quiet arrival.
senses.whyCN: 季节无论有没有人等待都会来，诗歌便用这个古老的名词指那种安静的来临。

intro.en: Advent is the Latin noun adventus, an arrival, from advenire, to come to, built on venire, to come.
intro.cn: advent 是拉丁名词 adventus「到达」，来自 advenire「来到」，其基础是 venire「来」。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it also feeds English venue, avenue and prevent.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，英语的 venue、avenue 与 prevent 也由它而来。

items.en: Ad plus venire gave advenire, to come to or arrive at a place.
items.cn: ad 加 venire 构成 advenire，意为「来到」或「抵达某地」。

items.en: The fourth-declension noun adventus named the arrival itself, whether of a person, a season or a god.
items.cn: 第四变格名词 adventus 命名到达本身，无论到的是人、季节还是神。

items.en: Old French took the word as avent, and English borrowed it first in ecclesiastical texts.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带作 avent，英语最先在教会文本中借入。

items.en: The liturgical sense is the earliest in English; the general sense of any arrival develops later.
items.cn: 英语中最早的义项是礼仪上的节期，泛指的「任何到来」则发展得较晚。

items.en: Modern usage splits the lowercase general noun from the capitalised season, a distinction kept in print.
items.cn: 现代用法把小写的泛指名词与大写的节期分开，印刷中一直保留这一区别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same venire family, two of which have drifted far from plain arrival; the near-meaning group gathers plainer words for coming, which differ in register and in what they name.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 venire 词族的词，其中两个已远离「到达」的本义；近义组收表示「来临」的更朴素说法，差别在于语体与所指。

entries.definition: From Latin adventura, things about to happen, but now meaning a risky journey rather than a coming.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」，但今义是冒险旅程，而非到来。

entries.definition: A botanical and medical adjective meaning arriving from outside rather than by nature.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学与医学形容词，指从外部而非本性带来的。

entries.definition: A member of a church that centres on the expected second coming.
entries.definitionCN: 以期待基督再临为核心的教会成员。

entries.definition: The plain word for reaching a place, used of people and trains more often than of eras.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地的朴素说法，多用于人与列车，而非时代。

entries.definition: A general noun for something approaching, without the formality or grandeur of advent.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物临近的名词，没有 advent 的正式或庄重感。

entries.definition: The beginning of something unpleasant, especially a disease or winter.
entries.definitionCN: 不愉快之事的开始，尤指疾病或冬季。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb venire, the word family and the fixed phrases the noun forms in English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁动词 venire、这个词族，以及这个名词在英语中构成的固定短语。

normal.en: Venire means to come, and ad adds direction: advenire is to come toward, so advent is the coming.
normal.cn: venire 意为「来」，ad 加上方向：advenire 就是「朝这边来」，所以 advent 就是「到来」。

normal.en: Venire is also hiding in venue, avenue and prevent, all about coming or blocking a coming.
normal.cn: venire 还藏在 venue、avenue 与 prevent 里，都与「来」或「挡住来」有关。

normal.en: The standard frame is the advent of something: the advent of the internet, the advent of cheap sensors.
normal.cn: 标准框架是 the advent of 某物：the advent of the internet、the advent of cheap sensors。

normal.en: Capitalised, Advent is the four weeks before Christmas, counted with an Advent calendar.
normal.cn: 首字母大写时，Advent 是圣诞节前的四周，用降临节日历一天天倒数。

normal.en: Before the advent of is the phrase for the world that existed earlier.
normal.cn: before the advent of 是描述「更早那个世界」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a ship sighted from a cliff: first a dot, then a mast, then a whole hull.
abstract.cn: 想象从悬崖上望见一艘船：先是黑点，然后是桅杆，最后是整个船身。

abstract.en: An advent cuts history in two, which is why the word can name an age as easily as a gadget.
abstract.cn: 一次到来把历史切成两段，所以这个词既能命名一个时代，也能命名一件小器具。

abstract.en: The liturgical sense survives because waiting is still the shape of the season.
abstract.cn: 礼仪上的义项之所以留存，是因为等待仍然是这个节期的形状。

examples.en: The advent of online banking closed hundreds of small branches.
examples.cn: 网上银行的到来让数百家小分行关门。

examples.en: Before the advent of the railway, the journey took three days.
examples.cn: 在铁路出现之前，这段路程要走三天。

examples.en: The choir rehearses throughout Advent for the midnight service.
examples.cn: 唱诗班在整个降临节期间为午夜礼拜排练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文特」——阿德闻声而至：到来

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ venire（来）→ advenire「来到」→ 名词 adventus「到达」，英语作 advent，指重要事物的到来，也指圣诞节前的降临节。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advent all describe something crossing the horizon: an awaited thing, a new technology, the church season, the final return, a new era, a person's arrival, the onset of illness and the coming of spring.
sensesIntro.cn: advent 的八个义项都描述某物越过地平线：被等待的事物、新技术、教会的节期、最终的再临、新时代、某人的到任、病症的发作，以及春天的来临。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dot on the horizon growing until it is unmistakably here.
core.cn: 核心意象：地平线上的黑点不断变大，直到它确凿无疑地到了。

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL LINE: the plain coming and the first appearance of a tool are the same event seen close up.
branches.cn: 到来线：朴素的来临与一件工具的首次出现，是同一事件被拉近观看。

branches.en: THE SACRED LINE: the season and the second coming both turn waiting into a calendar.
branches.cn: 神圣线：节期与再临都把等待变成一份日历。

branches.en: THE EPOCH LINE: a large enough arrival becomes the name of an age.
branches.cn: 时代线：一次足够大的到来会变成时代的名字。

branches.en: THE ENTRANCE LINE: people and diseases alike make their entrance on the same noun.
branches.cn: 登场线：人与疾病都用同一个名词完成自己的登场。

branches.en: THE SEASON LINE: spring arrives without waiting, and the old noun still fits.
branches.cn: 季节线：春天并不等待谁就来了，而这个古老名词依然合用。

intro.en: Advent is a Latin fourth-declension noun from advenire; English keeps the -vent stem and builds -ist, -itious and -al on it.
intro.cn: advent 是来自 advenire 的拉丁第四变格名词；英语保留 -vent 词干，并在其上构成 -ist、-itious 与 -al。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and adventus are all attested in Latin, so the chain needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与 adventus 在拉丁语中均有文献，这条链条无需构拟。

items.example: It turns venire into a coming toward.
items.exampleCN: 它把 venire 变成「朝这边来」。

items.example: It is the semantic core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的意义核心。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It appears in advent, event and prevent.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 advent、event 与 prevent 中。

derivatives.zh: 由 Advent 加 -ist 构成，指「期待基督再临的教派成员」
由同一词根加 -itious 构成，义为「偶然外来的」

definition_zh: 不利的；有害的；反对的；相反的
definition_en: unfavorable to success or well-being, or opposed and contrary to something
core_image: 帆船正顺风前行，一股逆向的侧风突然把船身推离航线
scene: 登山队刚出发不久，山脊上就压来一片铅灰色的云。The climb was called off because of adverse weather.
sceneCN: 这里的 adverse 是「不利的」（第 1 个义项：对顺利与安全有害的）；句意为由于天气恶劣，攀登被取消。

pos.zh: 形容词：不利的；有害的；反对的；相反的

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不利地；有害地」
由同一词根构成，义为「逆境；不幸」
由拉丁语 adversarius 而来，义为「对手；敌手」
加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「对抗性的」

senses.title: Against one's interests
senses.definition: harmful to success, health, or well-being, or making a good result less likely
senses.definitionCN: 对成功、健康或福祉有害的，或使好结果更难出现的
senses.example: Heavy rain had an adverse effect on the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨对收成产生了不利影响。
senses.why: ad- means towards and vertere means to turn, so adversus is 'turned towards' in a hostile way: an adverse force has turned round to face you.
senses.whyCN: ad- 表示朝向，vertere 表示转，adversus 是「转过来对着」，即掉头冲着你来的力量，所以 adverse 指不利。

senses.title: Opposed in opinion
senses.definition: not in favour of a plan, proposal, or position, and acting or speaking against it
senses.definitionCN: 不赞成某项计划、提议或立场的，并加以反对的
senses.example: The board remained adverse to any rise in membership fees.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会仍然反对提高任何会员费。
senses.why: The same turning image moves from events to the will: when someone is adverse to a proposal, their attitude has swung round to face it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「转身」的意象从事件转到意志上：说一个人 adverse to 某提议，就是他的态度已转过来对着它。

intro.en: One Latin verb of turning grows into a word for whatever turns against us.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，长成了指称「掉头与我们作对之物」的词。

items.en: vertere meant to turn, and it underlies a large family: versus, reverse, convert and vertigo all turn in some way.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，它支撑起一大族词：versus、reverse、convert 与 vertigo 都带「转」的意思。

items.en: ad 'towards' plus versum 'turned' gave adversum, a phrase meaning 'towards, facing', which could turn hostile.
items.cn: ad（向）加 versum（转过的）构成 adversum，本指「朝向、面对」，也可以带出敌对的意味。

items.en: As an adjective adversus meant 'opposite, contrary, hostile'; as a noun, an adversary was the person facing you.
items.cn: 作形容词时 adversus 意为「对面的、相反的、敌对的」；作名词时指「面对着你的人」，即敌手。

items.en: Old French passed the adjective into English in the sense of contrary fortune or opposing circumstance.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词传入英语，当时多指「相反遭际」或「对立情形」。

items.en: English records adverse from the fourteenth century; the modern phrase adverse effect dates from later technical writing.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起记录 adverse；现代常用的 adverse effect 则来自较晚的专业文献。

items.en: Today the word is most at home before nouns such as effect, weather and reaction, marking whatever works against a good outcome.
items.cn: 今天它最常放在 effect、weather、reaction 这类名词前，标记一切与好结果作对的因素。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root of turning; the second collects common words for what works against us.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「转」的拉丁词根；第二组收几个表示「与人作对」的常用词。

entries.definition: a difficult or unlucky situation; misfortune
entries.definitionCN: 逆境；不幸的处境

entries.definition: an opponent in an argument, contest, or conflict
entries.definitionCN: 对手；敌手

entries.definition: in a way that harms or works against something
entries.definitionCN: 不利地；有害地

entries.definition: to turn away or prevent something bad; same turning root, other prefix
entries.definitionCN: 避免；转移；同词根但前缀不同

entries.definition: not likely to produce a good result; the plain opposite of favourable
entries.definitionCN: 不利的；不妙的；favourable 的反义词

entries.definition: causing damage, especially to health; more physical than adverse
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；尤指对健康造成损害，比 adverse 更具体

entries.definition: openly unfriendly or opposed; stronger in feeling than adverse
entries.definitionCN: 敌对的；敌意的；情绪比 adverse 更强烈

entries.definition: causing harm or damage; a formal synonym common in reports
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；造成损害的；报告体常用

normalIntro.en: Three real pieces carry the word: ad-, vertere and the adjective ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由三个真实部件构成：ad-、vertere 与形容词词尾。

normal.en: ad- is towards and vertere is to turn, so adverse is turned against you.
normal.cn: ad- 是「朝向」，vertere 是「转」，adverse 就是转过来对着你。

normal.en: The same root gives versus, reverse and convert, all words of turning.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 versus、reverse、convert，都是「转」的词。

normal.en: adverse effect is the commonest pairing in medical and business writing.
normal.cn: adverse effect 是医学与商业文本里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Do not confuse adverse with averse; averse describes a person's dislike.
normal.cn: 别把 adverse 与 averse 混用，averse 说的是人「不喜欢」。

normal.en: Spell it with -verse, the same ending as reverse.
normal.cn: 拼写是 -verse，和 reverse 的结尾一样。

abstract.en: Picture a sail turning flat against the wind, and the boat losing speed.
abstract.cn: 想象帆面转过来迎着风，船立刻慢下来。

abstract.en: See a row of arrows all pointing at one small figure on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一排箭头全部指向一个很小的人影。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that keeps swinging shut in your face, however often you open it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，你每推开一次，它都朝你脸上关回来。

examples.en: The drug may cause adverse effects in older patients.
examples.cn: 这种药可能在老年患者身上引起不良反应。

examples.en: Farmers struggled through a season of adverse conditions.
examples.cn: 农民在整整一季的不利条件中艰难支撑。

examples.en: She remained adverse to the idea of moving abroad.
examples.cn: 她仍然反对搬到国外去的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃斯」——爱德沃斯一遇逆风就掉头，处处跟他作对。

root: 拉丁语 adversus 由 ad-「朝向」与 vertere「转」构成，本义是「转过来对着、敌对的」，经古法语进入英语后专指「不利的、相反的」。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one image of turning: circumstances turn against you, or a person's will turns against a proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用一个「转身」的意象：要么环境掉头与你作对，要么人的意志掉头反对某项提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sail swings round and faces the wind, and the boat loses way.
core.cn: 核心意象：帆面转过来迎风，船随即失去速度。

branches.en: weather that pushes a climb off its route
branches.cn: 把登山计划推离路线的天气

branches.en: a vote that swings against a proposal
branches.cn: 转而反对提案的表决

branches.en: a drug acting against the body it should help
branches.cn: 与身体作对的药物

branches.en: a fixed hostile stance in a debate
branches.cn: 辩论中固定的敌对立场

branches.en: one turning root, used for events and for attitudes
branches.cn: 同一个「转」的词根，既用于事件也用于态度

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of turning, and ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，加上普通的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: vertere and adversus are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 与 adversus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，只有更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 逆境；厄运；苦难；不幸
definition_en: a difficult or unpleasant situation, especially one caused by misfortune
core_image: 车轮陷进泥里，越用力反而越往下沉
scene: 暴雨后的乡道上，一辆卡车陷在泥里，司机蹲在轮胎旁抽烟。He learned patience in adversity, not in comfort.
sceneCN: 这里 adversity 是「逆境」（第 1 个义项：由不幸造成的困难处境）；句意为他在逆境中学会了耐心，而不是在安逸里。图中可辨识的物件：泥浆、轮胎、烟头。

pos.zh: 逆境；厄运；苦难（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 本名词的形容词基础，义为「不利的；有害的」
由 adverse 加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」
由同一词干加 -ative 构成，语法术语，指「表示转折的（词）」

senses.title: A difficult situation caused by misfortune
senses.definition: a hard or unfavourable situation brought about by bad luck or misfortune
senses.definitionCN: 由坏运气或不幸造成的一种艰难或不利处境
senses.example: The family stayed together through years of adversity.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人历经多年逆境仍守在一起。
senses.why: The noun is built on adverse, turned against, so adversity is the condition of living with things turned against you.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建于 adverse「转向对立」之上，所以 adversity 就是生活在「事物都与你作对」的处境里。

senses.title: Hardship as a continuing condition
senses.definition: as a mass noun, prolonged suffering and difficulty rather than one event
senses.definitionCN: 作不可数名词时，指长期的煎熬与艰难，而非单一事件
senses.example: Adversity had worn the patience of the whole village thin.
senses.exampleCN: 苦难把整个村子的耐心都磨薄了。
senses.why: When the turned-against condition lasts, it stops being an incident and becomes a climate.
senses.whyCN: 当「与你作对」的处境持续下去，它就不再是一件事，而变成一种气候。

senses.title: A particular calamity
senses.definition: a specific misfortune that can be counted among others
senses.definitionCN: 可以和其他不幸并列计数的一次具体灾祸
senses.example: They survived three adversities in a single winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在同一个冬天里扛过了三场灾祸。
senses.why: The countable use treats each misfortune as a separate blow, which is why the plural is possible.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法把每一次不幸当作单独的一击，所以这个词可以有复数。

senses.title: Financial distress
senses.definition: an older use for poverty or a lack of money and means
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指贫困或缺少钱财与生计手段
senses.example: The letters describe the adversity of a family without rent money.
senses.exampleCN: 这些书信描述了一个连房租都拿不出的家庭的困窘。
senses.why: Money is the commonest form in which things turn against a household, so the word often means plain poverty.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是一个家庭最常遭遇的「作对」形式，所以这个词常直接指贫困。

senses.title: The emotional strain of hardship
senses.definition: the inner strain produced by living through difficult conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在艰难处境中生活所产生的内心压力
senses.example: Adversity can isolate a person even in a crowded room.
senses.exampleCN: 逆境能让人即使身处满屋人也感到孤立。
senses.why: External conditions are also felt inside, so the noun can name the weight rather than the circumstance.
senses.whyCN: 外部处境也会被从内部感受到，所以这个名词能命名那份重量，而非处境本身。

senses.title: A test of character
senses.definition: hardship understood as a trial that reveals what a person is made of
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为揭示一个人本性的试炼的艰难
senses.example: Adversity shows which friendships are merely convenient.
senses.exampleCN: 逆境会显出哪些友谊只是图方便。
senses.why: A force turned against you also tests you, and moral writing has long used the word for that examination.
senses.whyCN: 一股对着你的力量也在考验你，道德文章早就用这个词来指那场考试。

senses.title: Hostile opposition
senses.definition: in formal or older writing, active hostility or opposition from others
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或较旧的文字中，指他人主动的敌意或阻挠
senses.example: The reform met adversity from every landed interest.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革遭到每一个地主利益的阻挠。
senses.why: Adversity can be people rather than events, because people are the ones who turn against a cause.
senses.whyCN: 逆境可以是人，而不只是事件，因为正是人转向一项事业的对立面。

senses.title: The measure of true friends
senses.definition: in proverbial style, the condition in which loyalty is proved or exposed
senses.definitionCN: 在谚语式表达中，忠诚被证明或暴露出来的那种处境
senses.example: A friend in adversity is worth ten at the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 逆境中的一个朋友，胜过宴席上的十个。
senses.why: Proverbs compress the test sense into a social lesson, and the word becomes a yardstick for people.
senses.whyCN: 谚语把「试炼」义压缩成一句人情教训，这个词于是成了衡量人的尺子。

intro.en: Adversity is the Latin noun adversitas, from adversus, turned against, itself the participle of advertere.
intro.cn: adversity 是拉丁名词 adversitas，来自 adversus「转向对立面的」，而 adversus 又是 advertere 的分词。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, the root shared by reverse, convert and vertigo.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，reverse、convert 与 vertigo 共享这个词根。

items.en: The participle adversus meant turned against, facing you as an obstacle or an enemy.
items.cn: 分词 adversus 意为「转向对立」，作为障碍或敌人面对着你。

items.en: The abstract noun adversitas named the state of having things turned against one.
items.cn: 抽象名词 adversitas 命名「事物都与自己作对」的状态。

items.en: Old French carried the abstract noun toward English as aversete and later adversite.
items.cn: 古法语把这个抽象名词带向英语，先作 aversete，后作 adversite。

items.en: English records the noun in the fourteenth century, mostly in moral and religious writing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录这个名词，多见于道德与宗教写作。

items.en: Modern usage keeps both the mass sense of prolonged hardship and the countable sense of a calamity.
items.cn: 现代用法同时保留「长期苦难」的不可数义与「一场灾祸」的可数义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same vertere family, including the trap averse, which describes reluctance rather than hardship; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for hard times.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 vertere 词族的词，其中包括陷阱词 averse，它说的是不情愿而非苦难；近义组收表示艰难时世的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for what works against you, from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容与你作对之物的形容词，这个名词正是由它构成。

entries.definition: An opponent, the personified form of what is turned against you.
entries.definitionCN: 对手，是「转向你之物」的人格化形式。

entries.definition: Unwilling or reluctant, a personal feeling with a different prefix, not a condition of hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 意为不情愿、反感，是带不同前缀的个人感受，并非苦难处境。

entries.definition: Suffering caused by difficult living conditions, often material and practical.
entries.definitionCN: 艰难生活条件造成的苦，常偏物质与实际层面。

entries.definition: Bad luck or a single unlucky event, usually shorter than adversity.
entries.definitionCN: 坏运气或单次不幸事件，通常比 adversity 更短促。

entries.definition: A great trial or suffering, with a strong religious or literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的试炼或苦难，带浓厚的宗教或文学语气。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the adversus root, the abstract -ity ending and the phrases adversity actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 adversus 词根、抽象名词词尾 -ity，以及 adversity 实际构成的短语。

normal.en: Adversus is turned against; add -ity and you get the state of being turned against.
normal.cn: adversus 是「转向对立」；加上 -ity，就得到「被转向对立」的状态。

normal.en: The adjective is adverse, the noun is adversity, and the person is an adversary.
normal.cn: 形容词是 adverse，名词是 adversity，而那个人是 adversary。

normal.en: The standard phrases are in adversity and overcome adversity.
normal.cn: 标准短语是 in adversity 与 overcome adversity。

normal.en: Do not confuse adversity with averse: one is hardship, the other is reluctance.
normal.cn: 不要把 adversity 与 averse 混了：一个是苦难，一个是不情愿。

normal.en: The plural adversities counts separate blows, as in three adversities in one winter.
normal.cn: 复数 adversities 数的是分开的打击，如「一个冬天里的三场灾祸」。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel spinning in mud: effort and sinking increase together.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在泥里空转的车轮：越用力，陷得越深。

abstract.en: Adversity is not one event but a direction, which is why it can also name a mood.
abstract.cn: 逆境不是一个事件，而是一个方向，所以它也能命名一种心境。

abstract.en: The proverb makes the word a test: what survives adversity is what was real.
abstract.cn: 谚语把这个词变成一场考试：熬过逆境的，才是真的。

examples.en: The company survived the adversity of two lost seasons.
examples.cn: 这家公司熬过了两个失收季节的逆境。

examples.en: In adversity she discovered who would actually answer the phone.
examples.cn: 在逆境中，她看清了谁会真的接电话。

examples.en: The memoir treats adversity as a teacher rather than a punishment.
examples.cn: 这本回忆录把逆境当作老师，而不是惩罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃西提」——沃西提陷在泥里越挣越深：逆境

root: 拉丁语 adversus（转向对立面的）+ 抽象名词词尾 -itas → adversitas，经古法语进入英语作 adversity，义为逆境、厄运与苦难。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adversity all come from things turned against a person: a hard situation, lasting hardship, a single calamity, poverty, inner strain, a moral test, human hostility and the proverb's yardstick for friends.
sensesIntro.cn: adversity 的八个义项都来自「事物转向一个人」：艰难处境、长期苦难、单场灾祸、贫困、内心重压、品格试炼、他人的敌意，以及谚语里衡量朋友的尺子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel sinking deeper the harder it turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：越用力转，陷得越深的一只车轮。

branches.en: THE CONDITION LINE: one hard situation, a lasting climate and a counted calamity are three scales of the same thing.
branches.cn: 处境线：一个艰难处境、一种持续气候、一场可数的灾祸，是同一事物的三种尺度。

branches.en: THE POVERTY LINE: lack of money is the oldest concrete form of hardship.
branches.cn: 贫困线：缺钱是苦难最古老的具体形态。

branches.en: THE INNER LINE: the outer condition is also felt as weight.
branches.cn: 内心线：外部处境也被感受为一种重量。

branches.en: THE TEST LINE: hardship reveals character and sorts friends.
branches.cn: 试炼线：苦难既显露品格，也筛出朋友。

branches.en: THE HUMAN LINE: sometimes the force turned against you is other people.
branches.cn: 人事线：有时转向你的那股力量，就是别的人。

intro.en: Adversity is adversus plus the abstract -ity; the family also gives adverse, adversely and adversary, all from the same vertere root.
intro.cn: adversity 是 adversus 加抽象词尾 -ity；词族还给出 adverse、adversely 与 adversary，全部来自同一 vertere 词根。

latinIntro.en: Vertere, adversus and adversitas are attested in Latin, so the derivation is documented.
latinIntro.cn: vertere、adversus 与 adversitas 在拉丁语中有文献，这条派生有据可查。

items.example: It turns the root toward an opposing direction.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词根转向对立的方向。

items.example: It is the shared root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族共享的词根。

items.example: It supplies the adjective and the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 它提供形容词与名词词干。

items.example: It is the direct source of adversity.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adversity 的直接来源。
它把 adversus 变成 adversity。
