由 adverse 加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」

definition_zh: 广告（英式口语）；提及、注意到（正式动词）
definition_en: a notice that promotes something, or in formal use, to call attention to a point
core_image: 街角橱窗里一张手写的小告示，把路人的目光拉过去
scene: 地铁站的柱子上贴着一张招租的小纸片。She spotted an advert for a flat near the station.
sceneCN: 这里的 advert 是「广告」（第 1 个义项：宣传某物的告示）；句意是她在车站附近看到一则公寓招租广告。

pos.zh: 名词：广告（英式口语，advertisement 的缩略）
动词：提及；注意到（正式用法，常与 to 连用）

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根构成，义为「做广告；宣传」
加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告宣传」
加 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」

senses.title: A public notice promoting something
senses.definition: a short public notice, especially in British English, that promotes a product, service, or vacancy
senses.definitionCN: 尤用于英式英语的简短公开告示，用来推介商品、服务或招聘岗位
senses.example: He answered a job advert in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他应征了当地报纸上的一则招聘广告。
senses.why: advert is simply advertisement cut short, so it keeps the idea of turning public attention towards something for sale.
senses.whyCN: advert 就是 advertisement 截短而来，因此保留了「把公众注意力转向某样待售之物」的意思。

senses.title: To refer to or mention
senses.definition: to turn one's attention to something in speech or writing; a formal verb usually followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作中把注意力转向某事；正式动词，通常后接 to
senses.example: The report adverted to the shortage of skilled staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告提到了熟练员工的短缺。
senses.why: The verb preserves the Latin sense of vertere, to turn: the speaker turns the listener's mind towards a topic.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词保留了拉丁语 vertere「转」的意思：说话者把听者的心思转向某个话题。

intro.en: A Latin verb of turning becomes first a French warning, then an English notice.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，先变成法语的提醒，再变成英语的告示。

items.en: vertere, to turn, is the root behind versus, reverse and convert as well as this family.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，除这一族词外还支撑 versus、reverse 与 convert。

items.en: advertere combined ad 'to' with vertere 'turn', meaning to turn the mind towards something, hence to notice.
items.cn: advertere 由 ad（向）与 vertere（转）合成，指把心思转向某物，因此有「注意」之义。

items.en: Old French avertir meant to warn or inform, and its noun avertissement meant a warning or notice.
items.cn: 古法语 avertir 意为「警告、告知」，其名词 avertissement 指「警告、通知」。

items.en: English took the verb advert in the sense of turning attention to something; the noun advertisement followed.
items.cn: 英语先借入动词 advert，表示把注意力转向某事；名词 advertisement 随后出现。

items.en: In British speech advertisement was clipped to advert, while the full verb survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 英式口语把 advertisement 截短为 advert；完整的动词则主要留在正式书面语里。

note.en: The first group is the advertising family; the second gathers words that mean a notice or a mention.
note.cn: 第一组是广告词族；第二组收表示「告示」或「提及」的词。

entries.definition: to promote goods or a vacancy publicly
entries.definitionCN: 做广告；公开宣传

entries.definition: the full noun for a public promotion
entries.definitionCN: 广告（完整名词形式）

entries.definition: the business or activity of promoting things
entries.definitionCN: 广告业；广告活动

entries.definition: to turn away or prevent; shares the turning root
entries.definitionCN: 避免；转移；共享「转」的词根

entries.definition: a sign or announcement giving information
entries.definitionCN: 告示；通知

entries.definition: a formal public statement about something
entries.definitionCN: 公告；正式声明

entries.definition: an advertisement on television or radio
entries.definitionCN: 广播电视广告

entries.definition: a brief reference to something in speech or writing
entries.definitionCN: 提及；简短说到

normalIntro.en: The word is advertisement with its tail cut off, built on a Latin verb of turning.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 advertisement 去掉尾巴，底层是一个表示「转」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: advert is advertisement shortened, so it means the same notice.
normal.cn: advert 是 advertisement 的缩短形式，指的仍是那则告示。

normal.en: The verb advert to means to turn attention to a point.
normal.cn: 动词 advert to 意为把注意力转向某一点。

normal.en: British speakers say advert where Americans say ad.
normal.cn: 英国人常说 advert，美国人常说 ad。

normal.en: A job advert sits in the classified pages of a newspaper.
normal.cn: job advert 出现在报纸的分类广告版面。

normal.en: The Latin root vertere, to turn, also hides in reverse and convert.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 vertere（转）也藏在 reverse 与 convert 里。

abstract.en: Picture a shopkeeper turning a handwritten card towards the passing crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象店主把一张手写卡片转向过路的人群。

abstract.en: See a finger turning a listener's face towards a detail on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指把听者的脸转向地图上的某个细节。

abstract.en: Imagine two uses of one motion: one sells a chair, the other points out a fact.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个转身动作的两种用途：一种卖椅子，一种指出事实。

examples.en: She put an advert in the window for her old bicycle.
examples.cn: 她在橱窗里贴了一则旧自行车出售广告。

examples.en: The magazine was full of full-page adverts.
examples.cn: 这本杂志里全是整版广告。

examples.en: He adverted to the delay only at the end of the meeting.
examples.cn: 直到会议结束他才提到延误的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃特」——爱得我特地贴张告示，把大家都叫来看。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「把心思转向」由 ad-「向」与 vertere「转」构成；经古法语 avertir「告知」进入英语，再由 advertisement 截短为 advert。

sensesIntro.en: Two uses of one turning motion: a notice turns the public towards goods, and a formal verb turns the mind towards a point.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「转」的动作有两种用法：告示把公众转向商品，正式动词把心思转向某个要点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handwritten card turned towards the crowd in a shop window.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里一张手写卡片转向人群。

branches.en: a card in a window pointing at a flat to let
branches.cn: 橱窗里指向待租公寓的卡片

branches.en: a newspaper column of posts waiting to be filled
branches.cn: 报纸上待招岗位的专栏

branches.en: a speaker turning listeners towards a shortage
branches.cn: 发言者把听众引向某个短缺问题

branches.en: a report that touches a risk in one sentence
branches.cn: 用一句话点到风险的报告

branches.en: the same turn, once towards goods and once towards a topic
branches.cn: 同一个转身，一次朝向商品，一次朝向话题

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of turning, and English endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，加上构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: advertere is recorded Latin; the French noun avertissement is the bridge into English.
latinIntro.cn: advertere 是有记录的拉丁词；法语名词 avertissement 是进入英语的桥梁。

items.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 咨询的；顾问的；警告性的；公告
definition_en: giving advice or a warning, or an official notice giving such advice
core_image: 一块贴在墙上的黄牌，牌上写着「请注意，前方有风」
scene: 气象台清晨挂出新告示，渔船纷纷回港避风。The coast guard issued a storm advisory before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 advisory 是「警告性的公告」（第 3 个义项：提醒危险的官方通告）；句意为海岸警卫队天亮前发布了风暴公告。

pos.zh: 咨询的；顾问的；警告性的

derivatives.zh: 动词基础形式，义为「建议；劝告」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「顾问」
同源名词，义为「建议；忠告」

senses.title: Giving advice in an official role
senses.definition: having the power or duty to give advice but not to decide
senses.definitionCN: 有权或负有义务提出建议但无决定权的
senses.example: She sits on the advisory board of a medical charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家医学慈善机构的顾问委员会任职。
senses.why: The Latin root videre means 'to see', so an advisory body is one that looks and tells, while others act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 videre 意为「看」，顾问机构就是负责「看并告知」、由别人去执行的机构。

senses.title: Warning of possible danger
senses.definition: giving advance notice of possible danger or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 提前告知可能有危险或麻烦的
senses.example: Pilots filed a flight plan around the advisory area.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员规划了绕开警报区的航线。
senses.why: Advice aimed at safety shades into warning: telling someone for their own good.
senses.whyCN: 为安全起见的「建议」滑向「警告」：为对方好而提前告知。

senses.title: An official notice or alert
senses.definition: an official announcement giving information, warnings or instructions
senses.definitionCN: 发布信息、警告或指示的官方通告
senses.example: The coast guard issued a storm advisory before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队天亮前发布了风暴公告。
senses.why: The adjective hardens into a noun: the warning itself becomes the thing named.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固成名词：警告本身成了被指称的事物。

intro.en: Advisory comes from advise, from Old French aviser, built on Latin videre, 'to see'.
intro.cn: advisory 来自 advise，后者经古法语 aviser 上溯拉丁语 videre（看）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- meant 'to see, to know'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为「看、知」。

items.en: Videre meant 'to see'; the wise man was one who had seen clearly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为「看」；智者即看得清楚的人。

items.en: Aviser meant 'to consider, to view', then 'to give counsel'.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「考虑、察看」，后转为「进言」。

items.en: Advise entered English as 'to give counsel'; advisory followed as the adjective.
items.cn: advise 于十四世纪进入英语，意为「进言」；advisory 随之成为形容词。

items.en: The word now spans advisory boards and official weather or travel advisories.
items.cn: 如今该词既指顾问班子，也指官方的气象或旅行警报。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same seeing root; the second gathers near synonyms of counsel and warning.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「看」词根的词；第二组收「劝告、警示」的近义词。

entries.definition: The base verb, to give counsel.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，advisory 的基础词，义为「建议」。

entries.definition: The noun of counsel; same root with a noun ending.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建议」；同根的名词形式。

entries.definition: The person who advises.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，提建议的人。

entries.definition: Relating to consultation and shared counsel.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「协商的、咨询的」。

entries.definition: An official brief announcement of news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公报」，指官方简短的新闻发布。

entries.definition: A warning signal of immediate danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警报」，指迫近危险的警示。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the seeing root and the yellow-notice scene; the abstract hooks picture watchers on the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「看」词根与黄牌场景；抽象记忆点想象墙上的瞭望者。

normal.en: Advise is the verb, advisory the adjective.
normal.cn: advise 是动词，advisory 是形容词。

normal.en: An advisory committee advises but does not decide.
normal.cn: 咨询委员会只进言不作决定。

normal.en: A travel advisory warns before you go.
normal.cn: 旅行警告在你出发前发出。

normal.en: The plural advisories names the official notices.
normal.cn: 复数 advisories 指那些官方通告。

normal.en: Latin videre, 'to see', is the deep root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看）是深层词根。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow card pasted on a harbor wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一张黄牌贴在海港墙上。

abstract.en: Picture a gray adviser whispering beside the throne.
abstract.cn: 想象灰袍顾问在王座旁低语。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse that advises, never commands.
abstract.cn: 想象只提醒、不发号施令的灯塔。

examples.en: The coast guard issued a storm advisory before dawn.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队天亮前发布了风暴公告。

examples.en: The committee has only an advisory role in policy.
examples.cn: 该委员会在政策上只起咨询作用。

examples.en: Officials posted a travel advisory for the flooded region.
examples.cn: 官员为受灾地区发布了旅行警告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额代在外」——额外交代一句「在外面注意安全」，这就是一句贴心的提醒公告。

root: 原始印欧词根 *weid-（看、知）→ 拉丁语 videre（看）→ 古法语 aviser（察看、进言）→ 英语 advise / advisory；核心义是「看得清，所以劝得了」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from counsel without power, to warning of danger, to the official notice itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从只有进言之权的顾问角色，到危险预警，再到官方通告本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a yellow notice that warns but does not command
core.cn: 核心意象：只警示、不命令的黄牌告示

branches.en: The board that looks and tells.
branches.cn: 负责察看与进言的委员会。

branches.en: The adjective that shades into warning.
branches.cn: 滑向警示义的形容词用法。

branches.en: The notice pinned where all can read.
branches.cn: 钉在人人可见之处的公告。

branches.en: Both senses inform without commanding.
branches.cn: 两个义项都只告知、不强令。

branches.en: Storms and travel alerts use this noun.
branches.cn: 风暴与出行警报都用这个名词。

intro.en: The word carries the seeing root vis- with the adjective ending -ory, and the family gives advise, advice and adviser.
intro.cn: 这个词带着「看」词根 vis- 与形容词尾 -ory，同族词有 advise、advice 与 adviser。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and avisus are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 videre 与 avisus 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 提倡者；拥护者；辩护律师；提倡、主张
definition_en: a person who publicly supports a cause, a lawyer who speaks for another, or the act of publicly recommending something
core_image: 法庭上紧挨被告站着的那个人，替他开口说话
scene: 社区会议上，居民们争论是否保留老图书馆。She advocated keeping the building open at weekends.
sceneCN: 这里的 advocate 是「提倡、主张」（第 3 个义项：公开支持某项做法）；句意是她主张周末继续开放这栋建筑。

pos.zh: 名词：提倡者；拥护者；辩护律师

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「拥护；倡导」
加 -or 构成，义为「拥护者」（较少用）
加 -ion 构成，义为「提倡的行为」（罕用）

senses.title: A public supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who publicly argues in favour of a policy, idea, or group
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某项政策、理念或群体辩护、争取的人
senses.example: She has long been an advocate of free school meals.
senses.exampleCN: 她长期以来一直是免费校餐的拥护者。
senses.why: Latin advocatus was one called to speak beside a person in court; the noun widened to anyone who speaks up for a cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 advocatus 指被叫到法庭上站在某人身边发言的人；名词后来扩大到任何为一个事业发声的人。

senses.title: A lawyer who speaks for another
senses.definition: a lawyer, especially in Scottish law, who presents a case in court for a client
senses.definitionCN: 尤指苏格兰法律中在法庭上替委托人陈述案情的律师
senses.example: The advocate rose to question the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师起身询问证人。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense kept alive: the courtroom figure whose whole role is to speak on someone else's behalf.
senses.whyCN: 这是保存下来最古老的义项：法庭上那个全部职责就是替别人说话的角色。

senses.title: To argue publicly for something
senses.definition: to recommend or support a policy or action publicly and often repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 公开且常常反复地推荐或支持某项政策或行动
senses.example: She advocated keeping the building open at weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 她主张周末继续开放这栋建筑。
senses.why: The verb turns the courtroom role into an activity: anyone can now stand beside an idea and speak for it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个法庭角色变成一种活动：如今任何人都可以站到一个理念旁边替它说话。

intro.en: A Latin word for a voice called to one's side, still audible in the courtroom sense.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词，本指被叫到身边来的声音，法庭义至今仍听得见这层本意。

items.en: vocare meant to call, and it gives vocation, vocal and vocabulary as well as this family.
items.cn: vocare 意为「呼叫」，它给出 vocation、vocal、vocabulary 以及这一族词。

items.en: ad 'to' plus vocare 'call' formed advocare, to call someone to one's aid, especially in a dispute.
items.cn: ad（向）加 vocare（呼叫）构成 advocare，意为「把某人叫来帮忙」，尤指争讼时。

items.en: The noun advocatus named the person called in to speak for another, the ancestor of the courtroom advocate.
items.cn: 名词 advocatus 指被叫来替别人发言的人，正是法庭上 advocate 的祖先。

items.en: Old French avocat carried the legal sense into English, where it named a lawyer pleading a case.
items.cn: 古法语 avocat 把法律义带入英语，指在庭上陈述案情的律师。

items.en: Since the eighteenth century the word has also worked as a verb meaning to speak publicly in favour of a cause.
items.cn: 十八世纪以后，这个词也作动词用，表示公开为一个事业发声。

note.en: The first group shares the calling root; the second gathers words for supporters and for speaking up.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「呼叫」的词根；第二组收表示「支持者」与「发声」的词。

entries.definition: public support for a cause or policy
entries.definitionCN: 拥护；倡导

entries.definition: one who advocates; a rare synonym of advocate
entries.definitionCN: 拥护者；较少见的同义词

entries.definition: a calling to a particular kind of work
entries.definitionCN: 职业使命；天职

entries.definition: a green fruit; only looks similar and comes from Nahuatl
entries.definitionCN: 鳄梨；只是拼写相近，源自纳瓦特尔语

entries.definition: someone who backs a person, team, or idea
entries.definitionCN: 支持者

entries.definition: a person who argues in favour of a proposal
entries.definitionCN: 主张者；支持者

entries.definition: to defend or support a cause actively
entries.definitionCN: 积极捍卫或支持

entries.definition: a general word for a legal professional
entries.definitionCN: 律师的通称

normalIntro.en: The word is built from vocare, to call: an advocate is called to someone's side.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 vocare「呼叫」构成：advocate 是被叫到某人身边的那位。

normal.en: ad- is to and vocare is to call, so an advocate is called to your side.
normal.cn: ad- 是「向」，vocare 是「呼叫」，advocate 就是被叫到你身边的人。

normal.en: The same root gives vocal, vocation and vocabulary.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 vocal、vocation 与 vocabulary。

normal.en: The noun stresses -cate, while the verb ends with a clear -ate sound.
normal.cn: 名词重音在前，动词结尾的 -ate 读得更清楚。

normal.en: An advocate of reform speaks for reform; the verb advocate reform does the same.
normal.cn: an advocate of reform 替改革说话；动词 advocate reform 做的是同一件事。

normal.en: A devil's advocate argues the other side just to test an idea.
normal.cn: devil's advocate 只为检验一个想法而故意站到对面。

abstract.en: Picture a figure standing shoulder to shoulder with the accused, speaking when the accused cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人与被告并肩而立，在被告说不出话时替他开口。

abstract.en: See the same stance outside court, beside a library or a policy rather than a person.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的姿态移到庭外，旁边不是人，而是一座图书馆或一项政策。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice called across a room simply to lend someone its strength.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音被叫过整个房间，只为把自己的力量借给某人。

examples.en: She has long been an advocate of free school meals.
examples.cn: 她长期以来一直是免费校餐的拥护者。

examples.en: The advocate for the defence asked for a short delay.
examples.cn: 辩方律师请求短暂延期。

examples.en: Several doctors advocated a ban on smoking in cars.
examples.cn: 几位医生主张禁止在车内吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃克特」——爱得我特地把他叫到身边，替我说句话。

root: 拉丁语 advocatus 由 ad-「向」与 vocare「呼叫」构成，本指被叫来替人发言者；经古法语 avocat 进入英语，先指辩护律师，后引申为「拥护者」与动词「提倡」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses keep one scene: someone called to stand beside another and speak for them, in court, for a cause, or as an act.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共守一个场景：被叫来站在别人身旁替他说话——在法庭上、为一个事业，或作为一个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing shoulder to shoulder with the accused, speaking for him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人与被告并肩，替他开口。

branches.en: a campaigner speaking for free school meals
branches.cn: 为免费校餐发声的倡导者

branches.en: a Scottish lawyer questioning a witness
branches.cn: 询问证人的苏格兰辩护律师

branches.en: residents arguing to keep a library open
branches.cn: 居民主张保留图书馆开放

branches.en: the campaigner and the campaign are the same stance
branches.cn: 倡导者与倡导行动是同一种姿态

branches.en: a voice called to the side of a person, a cause, or a proposal
branches.cn: 被叫到一个人、一个事业或一项提议旁边的声音

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of calling, and English noun and verb endings.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「呼叫」的拉丁动词，加上英语的名词与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: vocare, advocare and advocatus are recorded Latin; avocat is the French stage.
latinIntro.cn: vocare、advocare 与 advocatus 都是有记录的拉丁词；avocat 是法语阶段。

items.meaning: one called to speak for another

latinEntries.meaning: one called to speak for another

definition_zh: 充气；通气；使暴露于空气
definition_en: to introduce air into a material or substance
core_image: 园艺叉插进草坪再拔起，留下一排透气的小孔
scene: 园丁推着打孔机在草坪上来回走，泥土里冒出细孔。They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 aerate 是「给土壤通气」（第 1 个义项：把空气引入某物）；句意为他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「通气；充气」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「充气器；打孔机」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「充了气的」

senses.title: Introduce air into soil or material
senses.definition: to force air into soil, compost or another material
senses.definitionCN: 把空气压入土壤、堆肥或其他材料中
senses.example: They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。
senses.why: Greek aer means 'air', so the verb is literally 'to put air into'.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」，所以这个动词字面上就是「把空气放进去」。

senses.title: Charge a liquid with gas
senses.definition: to add carbon dioxide or another gas to a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 往液体里加入二氧化碳或其他气体
senses.example: The bar served aerated water with strong bubbles.
senses.exampleCN: 酒吧供应气泡很足的充气水。
senses.why: Air in the first sense generalizes to any gas stirred into a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的「空气」扩展为搅入液体的任何气体。

senses.title: Expose to fresh air
senses.definition: to let fresh air move through a space or substance
senses.definitionCN: 让新鲜空气在空间或物质中流通
senses.example: Open the windows to aerate the room after painting.
senses.exampleCN: 刷完漆后开窗给房间换换气。
senses.why: Putting air in implies letting air through: the material is opened to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 「放进空气」也意味着「让空气通过」：让物质向大气敞开。

intro.en: Aerate comes from Greek aer, 'air', joined to the Latin verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: aerate 由希腊语 aer（空气）加拉丁语动词尾 -ate 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wer- is linked to words for rising air and wind.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wer- 与表示升腾之气和风的词相关联。

items.en: Aer meant 'air, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」。

items.en: Scientific Latin aeratus meant 'charged with air', coined for chemistry.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语 aeratus 意为「充了气的」，为化学而造。

items.en: English formed aerate in the eighteenth century for chemistry and brewing.
items.cn: 英语于十八世纪造出 aerate，用于化学与酿造。

items.en: The verb now spans lawns, aquariums, wines and fizzy drinks.
items.cn: 如今该动词覆盖草坪、水族箱、醒酒与气泡饮料。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same air root; the second gathers related breathing and gas words.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「空气」词根的词；第二组收与呼吸、气体相关的词。

entries.definition: Of the air or an antenna; shares Greek aer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「空中的；天线」；同享希腊语 aer 词根。

entries.definition: Tiny particles or gas in a spray; the sol- half means 'solution'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气溶胶；喷雾」；前半同为 aer，后半 sol 意为「溶液」。

entries.definition: Requiring oxygen; built on the same air root with bios, 'life'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「需氧的」；同用 air 词根加 bios（生命）。

entries.definition: To move fresh air through a space.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通风」，让空气在空间中流动。

entries.definition: To add oxygen to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供氧；加氧」。

entries.definition: To charge a drink with carbon dioxide.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使充二氧化碳」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air root and the lawn-fork scene; the abstract hooks picture bubbles and open windows.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气」词根与草坪打孔场景；抽象记忆点想象气泡与敞开的窗。

normal.en: Greek aer means 'air'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」。

normal.en: Aeration is the noun, aerator the tool.
normal.cn: aeration 是名词，aerator 是工具。

normal.en: Aerated water is full of bubbles.
normal.cn: 充气水里全是气泡。

normal.en: Aerate the lawn by punching holes.
normal.cn: 给草坪打孔就是 aerate。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks it as a verb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标明它是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a fork lifting plugs of green turf.
abstract.cn: 想象草叉撬起一块块绿草皮。

abstract.en: Picture bubbles racing up a glass of soda.
abstract.cn: 想象气泡在一杯汽水里竞相上蹿。

abstract.en: Picture a stuffy room breathing again.
abstract.cn: 想象一间闷室重新呼吸起来。

examples.en: They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
examples.cn: 他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。

examples.en: Aerate the wine for a few minutes before serving.
examples.cn: 上桌前先给红酒醒几分钟气。

examples.en: Fish-tank pumps aerate the water all night.
examples.cn: 鱼缸气泵整夜给水增氧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 air »瑞特」——空气 air 被「瑞特」地塞进去，就是充气、通气。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）→ 新拉丁语 aeratus（充气的）→ 英语 aerate；核心义是「把空气送进东西里」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from aerating soil, to charging liquids with gas, to airing out spaces.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从给土壤通气，到给液体充气，再到给空间换气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air pushed into something dense until it breathes
core.cn: 核心意象：把空气压进密实之物，让它重新呼吸

branches.en: Holes punched so roots can breathe.
branches.cn: 打好孔让根系呼吸。

branches.en: Gas stirred into water or wine.
branches.cn: 搅进水或酒里的气体。

branches.en: Windows opened to moving air.
branches.cn: 向流动空气敞开的窗。

branches.en: Both senses let stale places breathe again.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让死气之地重新吐纳。

branches.en: Fizz is this sense's everyday face.
branches.cn: 气泡水是这个义项的日常面孔。

intro.en: The word carries the Greek air root aer- with the Latin verb ending -ate, and the family gives aerial, aerosol and aerobic.
intro.cn: 这个词带着希腊语「空气」词根 aer- 与拉丁动词尾 -ate，同族词有 aerial、aerosol 与 aerobic。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer via scientific Latin aeratus is the recorded ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的祖先是从希腊语 aer 到科学拉丁语 aeratus。

definition_zh: 空中的；航空的；空气的；（名词）天线
definition_en: relating to the air or to aircraft, or happening high above the ground; as a noun, a device that receives radio or television signals
core_image: 悬在半空的一根细线：既是空气，也是捕捉电波的天线
scene: 清晨的山谷里，摄影师的飞行器缓缓升空，镜头俯瞰着尚未醒来的村庄。The small drone took an aerial photograph of the valley at sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 aerial 是「空中的、从空中拍摄的」（第 1 个义项：与空气或空中有关）；句意为小型无人机在日出时拍下了山谷的鸟瞰照片。画面中可辨识：飞行器、山谷、晨雾。

collocations.zh: 鸟瞰；从空中看到的景象

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 aerial 加 -ly 构成，义为「在空中；通过航空方式」
由 aerial 加 -ist 构成，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人

senses.title: Existing in or relating to the air
senses.titleCN: 空气的；存在于空气中的
senses.definition: relating to the air or existing in it
senses.definitionCN: 与空气有关或存在于空气中的
senses.example: Aerial moisture turned the morning air into a thick mist.
senses.exampleCN: 空气中的水汽让清晨的空气变成了浓雾。
senses.why: Aer is the Greek word for air, and this adjective simply points to that element.
senses.whyCN: aer 是希腊语里表示「空气」的词，这个形容词直接指向这种元素。

senses.title: High above the ground
senses.titleCN: 高悬空中的；在空中发生的
senses.definition: happening or situated high above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 发生在地面上方高处的，或位于高处的
senses.example: An aerial cableway carried the tourists across the gorge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条空中索道把游客送过了峡谷。
senses.why: The same air becomes height: what is aerial is up there, away from the ground.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「空气」义进一步变成高度：aerial 的东西就在上方，远离地面。

senses.title: Done from or by aircraft
senses.titleCN: 航空的；从飞机上进行的
senses.definition: carried out from an aircraft, especially for photography or survey
senses.definitionCN: 从飞机上实施的，尤指摄影或勘测
senses.example: Aerial surveys mapped the damage after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，航空勘测绘制了受灾范围。
senses.why: Once the word moved from air to aircraft, work done in the sky became aerial work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从「空气」转向「飞机」，在空中完成的作业就成了 aerial 的工作。

senses.title: A device that receives signals
senses.definition: a metal device, often on a roof, that sends or receives radio and television signals
senses.definitionCN: 常装在屋顶、用于收发广播和电视信号的金属装置
senses.example: He climbed onto the roof to fix the aerial.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬上屋顶去修那根天线。
senses.why: An antenna stands up in the air to catch waves, so English reused the air word for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 天线竖立在空气中捕捉电波，于是英语干脆用「空气」这个词来称呼这个物件。

senses.title: Growing above the ground: aerial roots
senses.definition: of a plant part, growing above the ground rather than in the soil
senses.definitionCN: 指植物器官长在地面之上而非土壤之中的
senses.example: Orchids use aerial roots to absorb moisture from the humid air.
senses.exampleCN: 兰花用气生根从湿润的空气中吸收水分。
senses.why: Botany keeps the literal sense: the root lives in the air, not in the soil.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了最字面的意思：这种根生活在空气里，而不是土壤里。

intro.en: Aerial is built on the Greek word for air and entered English through Latin.
intro.cn: aerial 建立在希腊语表示「空气」的词上，经由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The noun aer meant 'air, mist, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 名词 aer 意为「空气、雾气、低层大气」。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer as 'air' and used it in both everyday and scientific writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 aer 表示「空气」，日常写作与科学写作中都在使用。

items.en: The adjective aerius meant 'of the air' and supplied the stem behind the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 aerius 意为「空气的」，为英语这个词提供了词干。

items.en: Aerial is recorded in the sixteenth century, first describing things in or of the air.
items.cn: aerial 于十六世纪见于记录，最初描述存在于空气中或与空气有关的事物。

items.en: In the twentieth century the noun aerial was applied to the antenna raised into the air for radio and television.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，名词 aerial 被用来指为收音机和电视竖在空中的天线。

note.en: The first group gathers words on the same air root or resembling aerial in spelling; the second gathers things that are airborne, overhead, or used to catch signals.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「空气」词根构成的词以及与 aerial 拼写相近的词；第二组收升空的、头顶上的或用于接收信号的事物。

entries.definition: To expose something to air or to force air into it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使暴露于空气；向……充气」，与 aerial 同出希腊语「空气」词根。

entries.definition: The nest of a bird of prey, built high on a cliff or rock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猛禽筑在高处岩壁上的巢」；只是拼写与 aerial 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A performer who works high above the ground, such as a trapeze artist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人，由 aerial 加 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: Carried in the air, or flying after leaving the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升空的；在空中的」，强调已经离开地面。

entries.definition: Above a person's head; in the sky directly above.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」，只强调相对位置，不涉及航空。

entries.definition: A device that sends or receives radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天线」，与 aerial 的名词义项所指同类物件。

normalIntro.en: Aerial can be recalled through its air root, its suffix, and its everyday collocations.
normalIntro.cn: aerial 可以通过「空气」词根、后缀以及常见搭配来记。

normal.en: Aer means air and -ial makes an adjective, so aerial is simply 'of the air'.
normal.cn: aer 意为「空气」，-ial 构成形容词，aerial 就是「空气的」。

normal.en: An aerial view is a view from the air, which fixes the adjective in a familiar phrase.
normal.cn: aerial view 是「从空中看到的景象」，这个常见搭配能固定形容词义。

normal.en: The noun aerial is the antenna that stands up in the air to catch waves.
normal.cn: 名词 aerial 就是竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

normal.en: Aerialist adds -ist to the same word and names a person who performs in the air.
normal.cn: aerialist 加 -ist，指在空中表演的人。

normal.en: Aerate and aerobic share the same air root, so the family can be learned together.
normal.cn: aerate 与 aerobic 共享同一「空气」词根，可以整族一起记。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire hanging above a valley, catching mist on one side and signals on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线悬在山谷上方，一边接住雾气，一边接收信号。

abstract.en: Think of a camera lifting off the ground: the higher it goes, the more the view deserves the name aerial.
abstract.cn: 想象相机离开地面升空：升得越高，眼前的景象越配得上 aerial 这个名字。

abstract.en: Link the word to wind on your face: air is the element behind every sense.
abstract.cn: 把这个词和风吹在脸上的感觉联系起来：空气是它所有义项背后的元素。

examples.en: The drone captured an aerial view of the flooded valley.
examples.cn: 无人机拍下了被洪水淹没的山谷鸟瞰图。

examples.en: He replaced the rusty television aerial on the roof.
examples.cn: 他更换了屋顶上生锈的电视天线。

examples.en: From the ridge, the village looked like a patch of colour in a green sea.
examples.cn: 从山脊望去，村庄像绿色海洋中的一小片色彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱瑞尔」——爱（ai）上空气，瑞（ri）尔（al）把它挂在高处，正好是悬在半空的细线。

root: 希腊语 aēr（转写为 aer）意为「空气」，拉丁语 aerius 是其形容词形式「空气的」，英语 aerial 由此而来，后缀 -ial 表示「与……有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start from the element air, rise into the sky, move to aircraft, and end with two concrete objects: the antenna and the air root.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「空气」这一元素出发，升到空中，转向航空，最后落到两个具体物件：天线与气生根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line suspended in the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根悬在空中的细线

branches.en: The literal element: what belongs to the air.
branches.cn: 本义：属于空气的事物。

branches.en: Height above the ground, where the air is.
branches.cn: 高度：位于地面之上的空中。

branches.en: Work done from aircraft in the sky.
branches.cn: 从飞机上进行的作业。

branches.en: The antenna that stands in the air to catch waves.
branches.cn: 竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

branches.en: The plant root that lives in humid air.
branches.cn: 生长在湿润空气中的植物根。

intro.en: Aerial is built from a Greek air root plus a Latin adjective ending, and its family is easy to map.
intro.cn: aerial 由希腊语「空气」词根加拉丁语形容词词尾构成，词族容易梳理。

latinIntro.en: Latin took aer from Greek and formed aerius 'of the air'; English borrowed the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 aer，并构成 aerius「空气的」；英语借用了这个形容词。

latinEntries.example: Aer is the source of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 是整个词族的来源。
aerius 在英语中变成了 aerial。

definition_zh: 飞艇驾驶员；气球飞行者
definition_en: a person who flies or navigates a balloon or airship
core_image: 一个人站在吊篮里，抓着绳索操纵漂在云上的气球
scene: 节日的草坪上空升起一只彩条热气球，围观人群仰头挥帽。The aeronaut waved from the basket as the balloon rose.
sceneCN: 这里 aeronaut 是「气球飞行者」（第 1 个义项：操纵气球或飞艇升空的人）；句意为气球升空时，飞行者在吊篮里挥手致意。

pos.zh: 气球飞行者；飞艇驾驶员

collocations.zh: 气球飞行者的黄金时代

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加 -ics 构成，义为「航空学」
由 aeronautics 派生的形容词，义为「航空的」
aeronautical 的变体，义为「航空的」

senses.title: Balloon or airship pilot
senses.definition: a person who operates or travels in a balloon or airship
senses.definitionCN: 操纵气球或飞艇、或乘其升空飞行的人
senses.example: The aeronaut waved from the basket as the balloon rose.
senses.exampleCN: 气球升空时，飞行者在吊篮里挥手致意。
senses.why: Greek aer, 'air', plus nautēs, 'sailor', makes the image literal: a sailor of the sky.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer（空气）加 nautēs（水手）字面拼出意象：天空的水手。

senses.title: Early aviation figure
senses.definition: an early experimenter in flight before powered aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 在动力飞机出现之前的早期飞行试验者
senses.example: Nineteenth-century aeronauts crossed the Channel in gas balloons.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的气球飞行者乘氢气球飞越了英吉利海峡。
senses.why: Before engines, the sailor-of-air image named the profession of those first airborne.
senses.whyCN: 在发动机问世前，「空中水手」的形象就是最早升空者的职业称呼。

intro.en: Aeronaut comes from Greek aer, 'air', and nautēs, 'sailor', first used in French as aéronaute.
intro.cn: aeronaut 由希腊语 aer（空气）与 nautēs（水手）拼成，最早以法语 aéronaute 出现。

items.en: The root *wer- lies behind air words; *nau- lies behind ship words.
items.cn: 「空气」词族背后是词根 *wer-；「船」词族背后是词根 *nau-。

items.en: Aer meant 'air'; nautēs meant 'sailor', as in nautes of naus, 'ship'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」；nautēs 意为「水手」，来自 naus（船）。

items.en: French coined aéronaute in 1784 for the Montgolfier-era balloonists.
items.cn: 法语于 1784 年为孟格菲兄弟时代的气球家造出 aéronaute。

items.en: English borrowed aeronaut as ballooning spread across Europe.
items.cn: 随着气球飞行风行欧洲，英语借入了 aeronaut。

items.en: Astronaut replaced it for space, while aeronautics keeps the stem in engineering.
items.cn: 航天时代由 astronaut 接棒，而 aeronautics 仍留在航空工程里。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same sailor root; the second gathers related flight people.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「水手」词根的词；第二组收其他飞行者称呼。

entries.definition: A space traveler; the naut half is identical, with astro- 'star' in front.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇航员」；后半 naut 完全相同，前半 astro- 意为「星」。

entries.definition: An underwater explorer; same naut with aqua 'water'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「潜水员；海底实验员」；同根 naut 加 aqua（水）。

entries.definition: A sailor of the ship Argo in Greek myth; the oldest of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「阿尔戈号船员；冒险者」；是这个家族里最古老的一员。

entries.definition: A person who flies balloons, the common modern term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「乘气球飞行者」，是现代常用说法。

entries.definition: A pilot of powered aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞机驾驶员」，指动力飞机的飞行员。

entries.definition: The general word for someone who controls an aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞行员」，泛称操纵飞行器的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air-plus-sailor root and the basket scene; the abstract hooks picture sails in the sky.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气加水手」词根与吊篮场景；抽象记忆点想象天上的帆。

normal.en: Greek nautēs means 'sailor'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 nautēs 意为「水手」。

normal.en: Aero- means air, so aeronaut sails the air.
normal.cn: aero- 是空气，aeronaut 就是空中水手。

normal.en: Astronaut is a star-sailor; aeronaut an air-sailor.
normal.cn: astronaut 是星际水手，aeronaut 是大气水手。

normal.en: Aeronautics is the science built on the stem.
normal.cn: aeronautics 是建立在该词干上的学科。

normal.en: Balloonists of old were called aeronauts.
normal.cn: 旧时的乘气球者被称为 aeronaut。

abstract.en: Picture a wicker basket drifting above rooftops.
abstract.cn: 想象柳条吊篮飘过屋顶上空。

abstract.en: Picture sandbags dropped to climb higher.
abstract.cn: 想象为了爬升而抛下的沙袋。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor's rope hands holding balloon lines.
abstract.cn: 想象水手般粗糙的手握着气球绳索。

examples.en: The aeronaut waved from the basket as the balloon rose.
examples.cn: 气球升空时，飞行者在吊篮里挥手致意。

examples.en: Early aeronauts needed calm winds and full gas bags.
examples.cn: 早期气球飞行者需要无风的天气与充足的气囊。

examples.en: The museum honors the aeronauts of the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆纪念十九世纪的气球飞行者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「air »闹」——在空气里「闹腾」的人，乘着气球上天玩杂耍的飞行者。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）+ nautēs（水手）→ 法语 aéronaute（1784）→ 英语 aeronaut；核心义是「驾驭气球这只天船的水手」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from piloting balloons and airships to the early pioneers of flight itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从驾驶气球与飞艇的人，扩展到最早的飞行试验先驱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sailor whose ship is the open sky
core.cn: 核心意象：以整片天空为船的航行者

branches.en: The hand on the balloon ropes.
branches.cn: 握着气球绳索的那只手。

branches.en: The pioneer before engines existed.
branches.cn: 发动机诞生之前的先驱。

branches.en: Both senses ride the wind without wings.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借风而无翼飞行。

branches.en: The basket is the aeronaut's deck.
branches.cn: 吊篮就是 aeronaut 的甲板。

branches.en: Their crossings opened the age of flight.
branches.cn: 他们的飞越开启了飞行时代。

intro.en: The word joins the Greek air root aero- with the sailor root -naut, and the family gives astronaut and aeronautics.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语「空气」词根 aero- 与「水手」词根 -naut 组成，同族词有 astronaut 与 aeronautics。

latinIntro.en: The combining parts are Greek; French aéronaute is the recorded coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分来自希腊语；法语 aéronaute 是有记录的造词。

definition_zh: 气溶胶；喷雾器；悬浮微粒
definition_en: a suspension of tiny particles in gas, or a pressurized container that sprays such a mist
core_image: 按下喷罐的喷头，细雾在光柱里悬浮不散
scene: 喷油罐一按，细雾在夕阳光柱里亮成一片。The painter wore a mask against the aerosol of lacquer.
sceneCN: 这里 aerosol 是「喷雾；悬浮微粒」（第 1 个义项：悬浮在气体中的细小颗粒）；句意为喷漆工戴着口罩抵御漆雾。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 aerosolize 加 -ed 构成，义为「雾化了的」
由本词加动词尾 -ize 构成，义为「使成气溶胶；雾化」
由 aerosolize 派生，义为「雾化过程」

senses.title: Particles suspended in gas
senses.definition: a mixture of fine solid particles or liquid droplets suspended in air or another gas
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮在空气或其他气体中的细小固体颗粒或液滴
senses.example: The painter wore a mask against the aerosol of lacquer.
senses.exampleCN: 喷漆工戴着口罩抵御漆雾。
senses.why: Greek aer, 'air', plus sol from 'solution', names literally a solution floating in air.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer（空气）加 sol（溶液），字面就是「悬浮在空气中的溶液」。

senses.title: Pressurized spray container
senses.definition: a metal container that uses gas pressure to release a fine spray
senses.definitionCN: 靠气压喷出细雾的金属罐
senses.example: Shake the aerosol well before spraying the paint.
senses.exampleCN: 喷漆前先把喷雾罐摇匀。
senses.why: The physics term extended by metonymy to the everyday can that makes the mist.
senses.whyCN: 物理名词经转喻扩展到制造雾气的日常罐子。

senses.title: Airborne disease transmission
senses.definition: tiny exhaled droplets that linger in air and can carry pathogens
senses.definitionCN: 呼出后长时间悬浮在空气中、可能携带病原体的微滴
senses.example: Ventilation reduces the risk from infectious aerosols.
senses.exampleCN: 通风能降低传染性气溶胶带来的风险。
senses.why: The same floating-particle image applies to droplets that stay airborne.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「悬浮颗粒」意象被用于久悬不落的飞沫。

intro.en: Aerosol joins Greek aer, 'air', with sol from solution, coined for colloid chemistry in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: aerosol 由希腊语 aer（空气）与 solution 的 sol 拼合，是二十世纪胶体化学的造词。

items.en: The root *wer- underlies the air word aer.
items.cn: 「空气」词 aer 背后是词根 *wer-。

items.en: Aer meant 'air, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」。

items.en: Solution and sol were standard chemistry terms for dispersed systems.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语中 solution 与 sol 已是表示分散系统的标准化学词。

items.en: Aerosol was coined around 1920 for colloidal particles in gas.
items.cn: 约 1920 年，aerosol 被造出，指气体中的胶体颗粒。

items.en: The word now covers spray cans, pollution science and virus research.
items.cn: 如今该词覆盖喷雾罐、污染科学与病毒研究。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same air root; the second gathers related suspension words.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「空气」词根的词；第二组收其他悬浮物相关词。

entries.definition: To introduce air; shares the Greek aer root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「充气；通气」；同享希腊语 aer 词根。

entries.definition: Of the air or an antenna; same aer root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「空中的；天线」；同根 aer。

entries.definition: Requiring oxygen; same aer with bios, 'life'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「需氧的」；同根 aer 加 bios（生命）。

entries.definition: A fine cloud of liquid droplets in air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄雾；水汽」。

entries.definition: Tiny solid particles suspended in air, as in pollution reports.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微粒；颗粒物」，常见于污染报告。

entries.definition: Liquid sent out in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「喷雾；喷洒」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air-plus-solution root and the spray-can scene; the abstract hooks picture floating glitter in a sunbeam.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气加溶液」词根与喷罐场景；抽象记忆点想象光柱里漂浮的微尘。

normal.en: Aero- is air; sol is from solution.
normal.cn: aero- 是空气，sol 来自溶液。

normal.en: An aerosol is a solution floating in air.
normal.cn: 气溶胶就是浮在空气里的「溶液」。

normal.en: Aerosol cans use gas pressure to spray.
normal.cn: 喷雾罐靠气压喷出雾来。

normal.en: Aerosolize is the verb for turning into mist.
normal.cn: aerosolize 是「使雾化」的动词。

normal.en: Virus research studies infectious aerosols.
normal.cn: 病毒研究关注传染性气溶胶。

abstract.en: Picture glitter hanging in a sunbeam.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光柱里悬停的金粉。

abstract.en: Picture a hiss and a fine cold cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象嘶的一声与一团细细的冷雾。

abstract.en: Picture dust motes that never seem to land.
abstract.cn: 想象久久不落的浮尘。

examples.en: The painter wore a mask against the aerosol of lacquer.
examples.cn: 喷漆工戴着口罩抵御漆雾。

examples.en: Aerosol sprays once used ozone-damaging propellants.
examples.cn: 气雾喷剂曾使用破坏臭氧层的推进剂。

examples.en: Scientists measured aerosols from the volcano.
examples.cn: 科学家测量了火山喷出的气溶胶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「air »瘦」——喷罐里的空气一按就「瘦」成细细的雾喷出来。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）+ solution 的 sol（胶体溶液）→ 英语 aerosol（约 1920，胶体化学造词）；核心义是「浮在空气中的细小溶液颗粒」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from suspended particles in gas, to the spray can itself, to airborne droplets in medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从气体中的悬浮微粒，到喷雾罐本身，再到医学上的空气传播飞沫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine mist hanging in a beam of light
core.cn: 核心意象：悬在光柱里不落的细雾

branches.en: Particles too light to fall.
branches.cn: 轻得落不下来的微粒。

branches.en: The can that makes the mist.
branches.cn: 制造雾气的那个罐子。

branches.en: Droplets that carry infection.
branches.cn: 携带传染物的飞沫。

branches.en: Both senses are matter riding the air.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是搭空气便车的物质。

branches.en: Household products use this meaning.
branches.cn: 日用品用的是这个义项。

intro.en: The word joins the Greek air root aero- with the colloid term sol, and the family gives aerosolize and aerosolized.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语「空气」词根 aero- 与胶体术语 sol 组成，同族词有 aerosolize 与 aerosolized。

latinIntro.en: The aero- half is Greek; sol is a modern chemistry coinage from Latin solvere.
latinIntro.cn: aero- 一半来自希腊语；sol 是由拉丁语 solvere（溶解）造的现代化学词。

definition_zh: 浮空器；气球（靠浮力升空的飞行器）
definition_en: a lighter-than-air craft, such as a balloon or airship, that stays aloft by buoyancy
core_image: 一只系着缆绳的大气球静静悬在山谷上空
scene: 边境哨所的山顶上，一只系留气球白天黑夜悬着值班。The aerostat hovered above the valley, tied by a long cable.
sceneCN: 这里 aerostat 是「浮空器」（第 1 个义项：靠浮力悬停的轻于空气的飞行器）；句意为浮空器拴着长缆悬在山谷上空。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「空气静力的；浮空的」
由 aerostatic 派生，义为「空气静力学」
历史用语，义为「浮空飞行术」

senses.title: Lighter-than-air craft
senses.definition: a balloon or airship that rises and stays aloft because its gas is lighter than air
senses.definitionCN: 因所充气体轻于空气而升起并悬停的气球或飞艇
senses.example: The aerostat hovered above the valley, tied by a long cable.
senses.exampleCN: 浮空器拴着长缆悬在山谷上空。
senses.why: Greek aer, 'air', plus statos, 'standing', names literally a craft that stands in air.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer（空气）加 statos（站立），字面就是「站在空气里的飞行器」。

senses.title: Ballooning as a practice
senses.definition: the art or practice of flying lighter-than-air craft
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶轻于空气飞行器的技艺或活动
senses.example: The museum traces the history of aerostat from Montgolfier onward.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展示了自孟格菲兄弟以来的浮空飞行史。
senses.why: The craft-name extends to the activity itself, as in older writers' aerostation.
senses.whyCN: 器物名扩展到活动本身，正如旧作家的 aerostation 一词。

intro.en: Aerostat comes from Greek aer, 'air', and statos, 'standing', coined in eighteenth-century French as aérostat.
intro.cn: aerostat 由希腊语 aer（空气）与 statos（站立）构成，十八世纪法语造出 aérostat。

items.en: The root *sta- meant 'to stand', and *wer- underlies the air word.
items.cn: 词根 *sta- 意为「站立」；「空气」词背后是 *wer-。

items.en: Aer meant 'air'; statos meant 'standing, set up'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」；statos 意为「站立的」。

items.en: French coined aérostat in 1784, right after the first balloon flights.
items.cn: 1784 年，首次气球飞行后不久，法语造出 aérostat。

items.en: English aerostat named balloons before aeroplane took over the sky.
items.cn: 英语 aerostat 曾是气球的称呼，后来 aeroplane 主宰了天空。

items.en: The term now survives mainly for tethered surveillance balloons.
items.cn: 如今该词主要用于系留监视气球。

note.en: The first group gathers same-root craft words; the second gathers related flying machines.
note.cn: 第一组收同根的飞行器词；第二组收其他飞行器名称。

entries.definition: Particles in gas or a spray can; shares aero- but names a mist, not a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气溶胶；喷雾」；共享 aero- 但指雾而非飞行器。

entries.definition: The adjective of aerostat, describing buoyant flight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，aerostat 的形容词形式，义为「浮空的」。

entries.definition: At rest; shares the Greek statos root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「静止的」；共享希腊语 statos 词根。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a lighter-than-air craft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气球」，日常说法。

entries.definition: A steerable lighter-than-air craft with engines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞艇」，可操纵、带发动机。

entries.definition: A small nonrigid airship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「软式小飞艇」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air-plus-standing root and the tether scene; the abstract hooks picture a balloon on a leash.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气加站立」词根与系留场景；抽象记忆点想象拴着绳的气球。

normal.en: Greek statos means 'standing'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 statos 意为「站立」。

normal.en: An aerostat stands in the air by buoyancy.
normal.cn: 浮空器靠浮力站在空气里。

normal.en: Aerostatic is its adjective.
normal.cn: aerostatic 是它的形容词。

normal.en: Tethered aerostats watch borders.
normal.cn: 系留浮空器用于边境监视。

normal.en: Aerostatics is the statics of buoyant air.
normal.cn: aerostatics 是研究空气浮力的静力学。

abstract.en: Picture a giant balloon held like a kite on a string.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被线拴住如风筝的大气球。

abstract.en: Picture gas straining upward against the cable.
abstract.cn: 想象气体向上挣、缆绳向下拽。

abstract.en: Picture an eye in the sky surveying all day.
abstract.cn: 想象整日巡视的天眼。

examples.en: The aerostat hovered above the valley, tied by a long cable.
examples.cn: 浮空器拴着长缆悬在山谷上空。

examples.en: Border patrols use radar-carrying aerostats.
examples.cn: 边境巡逻队使用搭载雷达的浮空器。

examples.en: Early aerostat flights thrilled all of Paris.
examples.cn: 早期浮空飞行让整个巴黎沸腾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「air »死搁」——气球「死搁」在天上不动，靠浮力一直悬停。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）+ statos（站立）→ 法语 aérostat（1784）→ 英语 aerostat；核心义是「站在空气里的浮空之器」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the buoyant craft itself to the practice of flying such craft.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从靠浮力悬停的飞行器本身，扩展到驾驶这类飞行器的活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon that stands still in the sky on a leash
core.cn: 核心意象：拴着缆绳在空中静立的气球

branches.en: The craft that floats without engines.
branches.cn: 不用发动机也能漂浮的飞行器。

branches.en: The old art of flying balloons.
branches.cn: 驾驶气球这门古老的技艺。

branches.en: Both senses live on buoyancy, not thrust.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠浮力而非推力。

branches.en: Surveillance is its modern job.
branches.cn: 监视是它如今的工作。

branches.en: Montgolfier opened this chapter.
branches.cn: 孟格菲兄弟开启了这一章。

intro.en: The word joins the Greek air root aero- with the standing root -stat, and the family gives aerostatic and aerostatics.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语「空气」词根 aero- 与「站立」词根 -stat 组成，同族词有 aerostatic 与 aerostatics。

latinIntro.en: The combining parts are Greek; French aérostat is the recorded coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分来自希腊语；法语 aérostat 是有记录的造词。

definition_zh: 审美的；美学的；有审美情趣的；美学；审美观
definition_en: relating to beauty and the judgment of taste, pleasing in appearance, or the set of principles behind a style
core_image: 美术馆里，一个人退后两步，眯起眼打量整面墙的构图
scene: 展厅里灯光很暗，参观者却迟迟挪不动脚。The gallery's aesthetic appeal drew crowds even on weekdays.
sceneCN: 这里的 aesthetic 是「审美的」（第 1 个义项：与美感判断有关的）；句意是这家画廊的审美吸引力连工作日都能引来人群。

pos.zh: 形容词：审美的；美学的；悦目的

derivatives.zh: 加 -s 构成，义为「美学（学科）」
由同一希腊词根构成，义为「唯美主义者；审美家」
加 -ally 构成，义为「在审美上；从美学角度」
加 -ism 构成，义为「唯美主义」

senses.title: Relating to beauty and taste
senses.definition: concerned with beauty, art, and judgments of taste rather than with usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 关涉美、艺术与品味判断，而不是实用性的
senses.example: The building has real aesthetic value, even if it is costly to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼确有美学价值，尽管取暖费用很高。
senses.why: Greek aisthetikos meant 'of sense perception'; the word moved from what the senses take in to the special pleasure of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aisthetikos 意为「与感官知觉有关的」；这个词从感官接收之物，转到美感带来的特殊愉悦。

senses.title: Pleasing in appearance
senses.definition: attractive or well designed in a way that shows good taste
senses.definitionCN: 在外观上悦目，或设计体现出良好品味
senses.example: The new bridge is aesthetic as well as strong.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥既结实又美观。
senses.why: When the adjective describes a thing rather than a study, it means the thing satisfies the taste that the first sense names.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词形容一件东西而不是一门学问时，它指该物满足了第一义项所说的那种品味。

senses.title: A set of principles of style
senses.definition: the ideas about beauty and style that shape a work, a movement, or a person's taste
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一件作品、一个流派或一个人品味的关于美与风格的理念
senses.example: The film's aesthetic owes much to 1970s photography.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的审美风格很大程度上借鉴了七十年代的摄影。
senses.why: As a noun the word names not beauty itself but the system of ideas that decides what counts as beautiful.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指的不是美本身，而是决定什么算美的那套理念系统。

intro.en: A Greek word about sense perception, made into a German science of beauty and then borrowed by English.
intro.cn: 一个关于感官知觉的希腊词，在德国被造成「美的学问」，随后被英语借走。

items.en: aisthesthai meant to perceive with the senses, to feel or notice something through the body.
items.cn: aisthesthai 意为用感官感知，通过身体去感觉或察觉。

items.en: aisthetikos meant 'of perception', concerned with what can be sensed rather than with pure thought.
items.cn: aisthetikos 意为「与知觉有关的」，关注可被感知之物，而非纯粹思想。

items.en: In the eighteenth century German writers made Aesthetik the name of a new discipline of beauty and art.
items.cn: 十八世纪德国作家把 Aesthetik 用作一门研究美与艺术的新学科之名。

items.en: English borrowed aesthetic from German, first as a term of philosophy and then of art criticism.
items.cn: 英语从德语借入 aesthetic，先作哲学术语，后进入艺术批评。

items.en: Everyday use now allows aesthetic to mean simply pleasing to look at, beyond its technical sense.
items.cn: 今天的日常用法让它超出专业范围，直接表示「看上去悦目」。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root of perception; the second gathers words about beauty and style.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「知觉」的希腊词根；第二组收关于美与风格的词。

entries.definition: the branch of philosophy that studies beauty
entries.definitionCN: 美学（哲学分支）

entries.definition: a person who cares greatly about beauty
entries.definitionCN: 审美家；唯美主义者

entries.definition: in terms of beauty or appearance
entries.definitionCN: 在审美上

entries.definition: a drug that removes feeling; same perception root, other prefix
entries.definitionCN: 麻醉剂；同词根但前缀不同，意思相反

entries.definition: relating to art or showing skill in art
entries.definitionCN: 艺术的；有艺术才能的

entries.definition: showing good judgment in beauty and style
entries.definitionCN: 有品味的；雅致的

entries.definition: pleasing to the senses; more emotional than aesthetic
entries.definitionCN: 美丽的；比 aesthetic 更带情感

entries.definition: relating to the manner of expression rather than beauty
entries.definitionCN: 风格上的；侧重表达方式

normalIntro.en: The root means perception: aesthetic is about what the senses judge as beautiful.
normalIntro.cn: 词根意为「知觉」：aesthetic 讲的是感官判定为美的东西。

normal.en: The Greek root aisthet- means perceive, so aesthetic is about felt beauty.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 aisthet- 意为「感知」，所以 aesthetic 关乎被感受到的美。

normal.en: An anesthetic removes perception; an aesthetic sharpens it.
normal.cn: anesthetic 去掉知觉，aesthetic 则磨锐知觉。

normal.en: Use aesthetically to describe how something looks.
normal.cn: 用 aesthetically 来描述某物看上去如何。

normal.en: An aesthete is a person who lives for beauty.
normal.cn: an aesthete 是为美而活的人。

normal.en: Spell it with ae-, and keep the th before the final -etic.
normal.cn: 拼写以 ae- 开头，结尾 -etic 前要先写 th。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor stepping back from a wall of paintings to judge the whole arrangement.
abstract.cn: 想象参观者从一整墙画前退后两步，判断整体布局。

abstract.en: See the same judgment applied to a bridge, where strength and shape must agree.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种判断落到一座桥上，强度与形状必须彼此相称。

abstract.en: Imagine the rules behind the judgment written down as a system of taste.
abstract.cn: 想象把判断背后的规则写成一套品味体系。

examples.en: The old factory has little aesthetic value but great historical interest.
examples.cn: 这座旧工厂没什么美学价值，却有很高的历史意义。

examples.en: Her garden is practical rather than aesthetic.
examples.cn: 她的花园重实用胜过美观。

examples.en: The designer explained the film's aesthetic in a short interview.
examples.cn: 设计师在简短访谈中解释了这部电影的审美取向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊斯赛提克」——伊斯在美术馆里退后两步，赛着看谁的品味更高。

root: 希腊语 aisthetikos「与知觉有关的」来自 aisthesthai「感知」；十八世纪德语把它造成研究美的学科名，英语随后借入，兼指「审美的」「悦目的」与「审美观」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move from the study of beauty, to a thing that satisfies it, to the system of taste behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从研究美的学问，走到满足这种学问的东西，再到它背后的品味体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visitor steps back to judge a whole wall of paintings.
core.cn: 核心意象：参观者退后两步，判断整墙画作。

branches.en: a listed building valued for beauty, not profit
branches.cn: 因美而非因盈利被珍视的登录建筑

branches.en: a question of taste rather than use
branches.cn: 关乎品味而非用途的问题

branches.en: a bridge whose shape pleases the eye
branches.cn: 外形悦目的桥

branches.en: a film borrowing the look of old photography
branches.cn: 借鉴旧摄影外观的电影

branches.en: perception, then pleasure, then the rules of pleasure
branches.cn: 先知觉，再愉悦，最后是愉悦的规则

intro.en: A Greek verb of perceiving, its adjective, and English endings.
intro.cn: 一个表示「感知」的希腊动词、它的形容词，加上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek; Latin borrowed it only as a learned term, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语；拉丁语只把它当作学术借词使用，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: of beauty; a system of taste

definition_zh: 和蔼的；亲切的；易于交谈的
definition_en: friendly, easy to talk to, and pleasant in manner
core_image: 一位长辈在门口笑着招呼每个进门的孩子
scene: 新店长站在门口，跟每位顾客点头问好。The affable manager greeted every customer by name.
sceneCN: 这里 affable 是「和蔼可亲的」（第 1 个义项：待人友好、容易接近的）；句意为和气的店长能叫出每位顾客的名字。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去 -ble 加名词后缀构成，义为「和蔼；亲切」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「和蔼地」

senses.title: Friendly and easy to talk to
senses.titleCN: 和蔼可亲的；易于攀谈的
senses.definition: showing warmth and good humor that makes conversation easy
senses.definitionCN: 待人温和幽默，使人乐于与之交谈
senses.example: The affable manager greeted every customer by name.
senses.exampleCN: 和气的店长能叫出每位顾客的名字。
senses.why: Latin affari means 'to speak to', so an affable person is one you can easily speak to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 affari 意为「对人说话」，所以 affable 的人就是容易与之搭上话的人。

senses.title: Gracious toward inferiors or guests
senses.titleCN: 对晚辈或客人谦和有礼
senses.definition: politely kind and condescending in a pleasant way to those of lower rank or to guests
senses.definitionCN: 对地位较低者或宾客表现出的客气与温良
senses.example: The old professor was affable with the youngest interns.
senses.exampleCN: 老教授对最年轻的实习生也和和气气。
senses.why: Speaking easily to anyone extends to speaking kindly downward the social ladder.
senses.whyCN: 「与谁都能谈」扩展为「对下也温和谈吐」。

intro.en: Affable comes from Latin affabilis, 'that can be spoken to', from affari, 'to address'.
intro.cn: affable 来自拉丁语 affabilis（可以与之交谈的），动词原形是 affari（对人说话）。

items.en: The root *bha- meant 'to speak', source of many speak-words.
items.cn: 词根 *bha- 意为「说」，是众多「言语」词的源头。

items.en: Fari meant 'to speak'; affari meant 'to speak to, to address'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fari 意为「说」；affari 意为「对人说话」。

items.en: Affabilis described a person you could approach and talk with.
items.cn: affabilis 形容一个可以接近并交谈的人。

items.en: English borrowed affable in the fifteenth century for easy, pleasant conversation.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入 affable，形容随和好谈。

items.en: Today affable paints friendly grandfathers, hosts and hosts of talk shows alike.
items.cn: 如今 affable 常用来写和气的长辈、主人与脱口秀主持人。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same speaking root; the second gathers near synonyms of friendliness.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「说」词根的词；第二组收「友善、随和」的近义词。

entries.definition: Too great to be spoken; the same fari root with in- 'not'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以言表的」；同一 fari 词根加 in-（不）。

entries.definition: Originally 'one who cannot speak'; shares fari.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婴儿」；本义「还不会说话的人」，同根 fari。

entries.definition: To influence; similar opening, unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响」；开头相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: Warmly cheerful and friendly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「亲切的；和煦的」。

entries.definition: Good-natured and likable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「和蔼可亲的」，强调好脾气。

entries.definition: Warmly welcoming, from the heart.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热诚的」，强调发自内心的热情。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the speaking root and the doorway scene; the abstract hooks picture easy talk and warm hellos.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「说」词根与门口场景；抽象记忆点想象轻松的攀谈与热络的招呼。

normal.en: Latin affari means 'to speak to'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 affari 意为「对人说话」。

normal.en: An affable person is easy to speak to.
normal.cn: affable 的人容易搭话。

normal.en: Ineffable shares the root: not speakable.
normal.cn: ineffable 同根：说不出。

normal.en: Affability is the noun of the quality.
normal.cn: affability 是该品质的名词。

normal.en: Affably describes the friendly tone.
normal.cn: affably 形容那副和气的语气。

abstract.en: Picture a host waving guests through the door.
abstract.cn: 想象主人笑着把客人往门里让。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled over for a chat.
abstract.cn: 想象为聊天而拉过来的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture wrinkles shaped by years of smiling.
abstract.cn: 想象被笑容刻出来的皱纹。

examples.en: The affable manager greeted every customer by name.
examples.cn: 和气的店长能叫出每位顾客的名字。

examples.en: His affable way put the new students at ease.
examples.cn: 他和蔼的态度让新同学放松下来。

examples.en: An affable host makes a party feel warm.
examples.cn: 亲切的主人让聚会倍感温暖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福」——人称「阿福」的人一脸福气、见谁都笑，特别和蔼。

root: 原始印欧词根 *bha-（说）→ 拉丁语 fari（说）→ affari（对人说话）→ affabilis（可交谈的）→ 英语 affable；核心义是「容易与之说话的人」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from easy conversation with anyone to gracious kindness toward guests and juniors.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从与谁都好谈，到对客人晚辈的谦和有礼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smile at the door that invites speech
core.cn: 核心意象：门口那副 inviting 你开口的笑

branches.en: The person anyone can talk to.
branches.cn: 谁都能与之攀谈的人。

branches.en: Kindness flowing down the ladder.
branches.cn: 向地位低处流淌的善意。

branches.en: Both senses make others feel welcome.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让人如沐春风。

branches.en: Small talk is this sense's home ground.
branches.cn: 寒暄闲聊是这个义项的主场。

branches.en: Hosts and professors typify it.
branches.cn: 主人与教授是其典型。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin speaking root -fab/-fess with the prefix af- and adjective ending -able, and the family gives ineffable and infant.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「说」词根 -fab/-fess、前缀 af- 与形容词尾 -able，同族词有 ineffable 与 infant。

latinIntro.en: Latin fari and affari are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 fari 与 affari 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 事情；事件；（复数）事务；风流韵事
definition_en: a matter or event, matters of business or public concern in the plural, or a secret romantic relationship
core_image: 书桌上一叠待办的文件，每一份都标着不同的名目
scene: 晚饭后，父亲把报纸摊开，皱着眉看国际版面。He followed foreign affairs long before he became a diplomat.
sceneCN: 这里的 affairs 是「事务」（第 2 个义项：复数形式指某一领域的事务）；句意是他早在成为外交官之前就关注国际事务。

pos.zh: 名词：事情；事件；事务；风流韵事

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「事务；业务」
同出拉丁语 facere「做」，义为「事实」
同出 facere，义为「结果；效果」

senses.title: A matter or event
senses.definition: a matter, situation, or event, often one that is being discussed or managed
senses.definitionCN: 一件被谈论或处理的事情、情形或事件
senses.example: The wedding was a quiet family affair.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是一次安静的家庭活动。
senses.why: Old French afaire literally meant 'to do': an affair is simply something there is to do or to deal with.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 afaire 字面就是「去做」：affair 就是一件有待去做、有待处理的事。

senses.title: Matters of business or public concern
senses.definition: in the plural, the business, interests, or public matters of a person, company, or country
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时，指个人、公司或国家的业务、利益或公共事务
senses.example: She handles the company's legal affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她负责处理公司的法律事务。
senses.why: A single matter is an affair, but a whole field of matters becomes affairs, the ordinary plural for business and government.
senses.whyCN: 单件事情是一个 affair，而一整个领域的事情就成了 affairs，这是商业与政务里的常规复数。

senses.title: A secret romantic relationship
senses.definition: a romantic or sexual relationship, especially one kept secret or outside marriage
senses.definitionCN: 浪漫或性的关系，尤指隐秘的或婚外的
senses.example: Their affair lasted only one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的恋情只维持了一个夏天。
senses.why: The neutral sense of 'a matter between two people' narrowed to the one matter people prefer to keep private.
senses.whyCN: 「两人之间的一件事」这个中性义，收窄成了人们最想保密的那件事。

intro.en: A French phrase meaning 'to do', worn down into a noun for anything there is to do.
intro.cn: 一个意为「去做」的法语短语，磨损成一个指「任何待办之事」的名词。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, and it gives fact, effect, factory and difficult as well as this word.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，它给出 fact、effect、factory、difficult 以及这个词。

items.en: The phrase ad faciendum, 'to be done', expressed work that lies ahead.
items.cn: 短语 ad faciendum 意为「有待去做」，指摆在面前的工作。

items.en: Old French contracted the phrase to a faire, 'to do', and used it for business or matters to attend to.
items.cn: 古法语把短语缩成 a faire「去做」，用来指事务或需要处理的事情。

items.en: Middle English borrowed afaire for a matter or business, then widened it to any event or concern.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 afaire 指「事情、事务」，后来扩大到任何事件或关切。

items.en: The plural affairs settled into politics and commerce, while the singular took on the romantic sense in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 复数 affairs 固定在政治与商业里，单数则在十八世纪发展出恋情义。

note.en: The first group looks alike but splits into different roots; the second gathers words for matters and relationships.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近但词根不同；第二组收表示「事情」与「关系」的词。

entries.definition: to influence or move someone; built on facere, to do
entries.definitionCN: 影响；打动；同样出自 facere

entries.definition: a result or change produced by a cause
entries.definitionCN: 结果；效果

entries.definition: the plural used for business and public matters
entries.definitionCN: 复数，指业务与公共事务

entries.definition: friendly and easy to talk to; a different root from affair
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；与 affair 词源不同

entries.definition: a subject or situation under discussion
entries.definitionCN: 事情；问题

entries.definition: work, trade, or matters that concern someone
entries.definitionCN: 事务；生意

entries.definition: something that happens, especially something notable
entries.definitionCN: 事件；大事

entries.definition: a love relationship, often idealised
entries.definitionCN: 恋情；浪漫关系

normalIntro.en: The word is a worn-down French phrase for 'to do', so it names whatever is to be done.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语「去做」磨损而来，因此指一切待办之事。

normal.en: a faire in Old French meant to do, and an affair is a thing to do.
normal.cn: 古法语 a faire 意为「去做」，affair 就是一件要做的事。

normal.en: The plural affairs is the normal word for business and politics.
normal.cn: 复数 affairs 是商业与政治的常规说法。

normal.en: Keep the double f and the -air ending together: affair.
normal.cn: 记住双 f 与 -air 结尾连在一起：affair。

normal.en: A love affair is the private version of a public matter.
normal.cn: love affair 是公共事务的私人版本。

normal.en: The same Latin facere hides in fact, effect and factory.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁语 facere 藏在 fact、effect 与 factory 里。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered with folders, each one a separate thing to be dealt with.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺满文件夹的书桌，每一份都是一件待处理的事。

abstract.en: See one folder lifted out and marked private, then locked in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象其中一份被抽出，标上「私密」，锁进抽屉。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole wall of folders turning into a ministry's business.
abstract.cn: 想象一整墙文件夹变成一个部门的公务。

examples.en: The whole trip became a complicated affair.
examples.cn: 整趟旅行变成了一件麻烦事。

examples.en: She was appointed to manage the city's financial affairs.
examples.cn: 她被任命管理这座城市的财政事务。

examples.en: The novel describes a long affair between two neighbours.
examples.cn: 这部小说描写了两位邻居之间的一段长久恋情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费尔」——阿费尔桌上摊着一叠事，公事私事都算一件事。

root: 古法语 a faire「去做」来自拉丁语 facere「做」，进入英语作 affair，本指「待办之事」，复数 affairs 专指业务与公共事务，单数后又衍生出「恋情」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one frame: something there is to do, whether a single event, a field of business, or a private relationship.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用同一个框架：一件有待处理之事，可以是单个事件、一片业务，或一段私人关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk covered with folders, each one a matter to handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺满文件夹的书桌，每份都是待办之事。

branches.en: a wedding kept small and quiet
branches.cn: 办得小而安静的一场婚礼

branches.en: a company's legal business
branches.cn: 公司的法律事务

branches.en: a diplomat reading the foreign pages
branches.cn: 外交官翻阅国际版面

branches.en: a summer relationship kept out of sight
branches.cn: 藏着的一段夏日恋情

branches.en: one 'thing to do', public or private
branches.cn: 同一件「要做的事」，或公或私

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing, worn down through French into a noun.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的拉丁动词，经法语磨损成一个名词。

latinIntro.en: facere is recorded Latin; a faire is the Old French contraction.
latinIntro.cn: facere 是有记录的拉丁词；a faire 是古法语的缩合形式。
